kitchen-renovation-quote-template.intro: This kitchen renovation quote template is for builders quoting standard residential jobs, from simple cosmetic updates to full gut-and-replace projects. It's designed to stop you from losing money on the two most common mistakes: underquoting on demolition and waste disposal, and forgetting to factor in making good on walls and floors after the old kitchen is ripped out. Get those two line items right, and the rest of the quote will fall into place, ensuring your price is both competitive and profitable for the work involved.

sections.heading: How to Price the Big Three: Cabinets, Benchtops, and Labour
sections.body: Your biggest costs are materials and time. Price cabinets per unit, not per metre. A standard 600mm base cabinet from a supplier like Polytec or Laminex might cost $300, but a drawer unit will be double that. For benchtops, quote per linear metre (lm). A laminate top from a trade supplier is around $150/lm, while an engineered stone benchtop can be $900/lm plus installation. Labour is the key. Your carpenter is likely on $70-$90/hr, your plumber $110-$130/hr, and your electrician the same. For a standard kitchen, budget at least 40 hours of carpentry, a full day for plumbing rough-in and fit-off, and another for electrical. Don't guess labour; track it.

sections.heading: What Everyone Forgets on a Kitchen Reno Quote
sections.body: It's the small things that kill your profit. Always include a separate line item for demolition and rubbish removal. A 4 cubic metre skip bin costs around $450, and that's before you pay someone to fill it. Is the site on the third floor with no lift? Add a site access fee for the extra labour. Making good is another one; plastering and painting where old splashbacks and bulkheads were removed can take a full day. Forgetting these costs is a classic error. A quoting app like QuoteMate can help by suggesting these easily-missed items from past jobs. All electrical work must comply with AS/NZS 3000, so factor in a licensed electrician for the final sign-off.

faqs.question: How much contingency do I add to a kitchen quote?
faqs.answer: For kitchen renovations, a 10-15% contingency is standard. This covers unexpected issues like rotten sub-floors hidden by old cabinets or finding asbestos in the walls. Clearly state in your quote what the contingency covers. For a $25,000 kitchen, that's a buffer of at least $2,500.

faqs.question: Should I quote for appliances or just the installation?
faqs.answer: Always clarify this with the client first. The safest way is to list appliances as a Provisional Sum (PS) or Prime Cost (PC) item. This allows the client to choose their own from a place like The Good Guys, and you just charge for the installation. If they want you to supply, get model numbers and exact prices before finalising the quote.

faqs.question: What's the difference in quoting for a tile vs. glass splashback?
faqs.answer: Tiled splashbacks are quoted per square metre for supply and labour. A simple ceramic tile might be $120/sqm installed. A glass splashback is a custom-made item quoted per piece, often with extra charges for each GPO cutout. A typical glass splashback costs between $450 and $650 per square metre.

concrete-driveway-quote-template.intro: This concrete driveway quote template is for Australian concreters pricing standard residential jobs. It covers new builds, extensions, and rip-and-replace projects. Getting the quote right comes down to two things often missed: accurate base preparation costs and accounting for concrete pump hire. Underestimate the earthworks or forget the pump fee on a site with poor access, and your profit is gone before the pour even starts. Use this template to make sure every cost is covered, from crushed rock to the final sealer, so you price every job to win and make a margin.

sections.heading: How to Price Concrete, Mesh, and Labour Per Square Metre
sections.body: Your biggest cost is the concrete itself. A standard 25MPa mix from a supplier like Hanson or Boral runs about $250-$320 per cubic metre. For a typical 100mm thick driveway, you'll need one cubic metre for every 10 square metres. Next is the steel. SL72 reinforcing mesh is standard for residential drives and costs around $110 per sheet from a trade supplier, covering roughly 14.4 square metres. Labour is the key variable. A good starting point is $60-$90 per square metre for a basic broom finish. Always add a 10% waste factor to your concrete and crushed rock calculations before finalising the price.

sections.heading: Forgetting Site Prep and Pump Hire Will Cost You
sections.body: The costs that get missed are usually before the concrete truck arrives. Site preparation isn't free. If you need to hire a mini-excavator to level the ground, that's at least $500 for the day. The crushed rock for the sub-base costs about $60 per tonne, plus your time to spread and compact it. If the truck can't back right up to the job, you'll need a concrete pump. A line pump adds a minimum of $600-$900 to the job. Also, remember to include tip fees for disposing of any excavated soil or old concrete. These small costs add up fast and should be separate line items on your quote.

faqs.question: How much extra should I quote for an exposed aggregate finish?
faqs.answer: Exposed aggregate costs more in materials and labour. The special concrete mix is dearer, and you have extra steps like washing off and sealing. You should add between $50 and $70 per square metre on top of your standard plain concrete price. Check current sealer prices with a supplier like Parchem or Concrete Colour Systems.

faqs.question: Do I need council approval for a new driveway crossover?
faqs.answer: Yes, almost every council in Australia requires a permit for a new or modified vehicle crossover from the kerb. While it's the homeowner's responsibility to get the permit, you should state in your quote that work cannot start without it. This protects you from fines and rework orders from the local council.

faqs.question: What's the right concrete strength for a residential driveway?
faqs.answer: For a standard driveway taking cars and utes, 25MPa is the industry standard and sufficient. If the driveway needs to support heavier vehicles like a small truck or the subgrade is poor, specify 32MPa. Always list the concrete strength on your quote to meet the requirements of Australian Standard AS 3600.

painting-quote-template.intro: This house painting quote template is for Aussie painters on residential jobs. It’s built for everything from a quick room refresh to a full interior and exterior repaint. Most quotes go wrong in two places: underestimating the hours needed for proper surface prep, especially on older homes, and miscalculating paint volumes for quality finishes. A cheap paint might save money upfront but costs you in callbacks. This template helps you price every surface, coat, and hour of labour correctly so your profit doesn't get painted over by unexpected costs.

sections.heading: Pricing Paint and Labour for a Standard 3-Bed House
sections.body: Your price comes down to materials and time. A standard 3-bedroom house has about 350-400 square metres of wall and ceiling space. Quality paint like Dulux Wash&Wear covers around 14 sqm per litre. For two coats, you'll need 50-60 litres. At roughly $220 for a 15L tin from a trade supplier, that's over $880 in paint before you add primer or trim colour. Labour is your main cost. A full interior repaint with proper prep takes 80-100 hours. At a rate of $60-$80 per hour, that's $4,800 to $8,000 in labour alone. Your quote must cover both accurately.

sections.heading: What Painters Forget to Add to the Quote
sections.body: Small omissions destroy your margin. Quoting a two-storey exterior without adding weekly scaffold hire can cost you $500 a week straight from your profit. Does the job involve removing old lead paint? That requires specific safety gear and disposal methods under AS/NZS 4361.2, adding significant time and material costs. Don't forget skip bin hire for waste, or the time it takes to move heavy furniture. If it's not a line item in the quote, you're doing it for free. Specify exclusions like major plaster repairs or electrical fixture removal to protect yourself.

faqs.question: How many coats of paint should I quote for?
faqs.answer: Always quote for a primer or undercoat, followed by at least two top coats. A single top coat rarely provides a durable or even finish, especially when making a big colour change. Quoting for two top coats is standard professional practice and ensures the job lasts. For covering dark colours or water stains, you may even need to factor in a third coat.

faqs.question: Should I charge per room or per square metre?
faqs.answer: Calculate your costs per square metre, but present the price per room to the client. Using a square metre rate for your internal calculations is the only way to accurately price materials and labour, especially for rooms with high ceilings or complex features. A simple per-room price is easier for the customer to understand on the final quote. Software like QuoteMate can handle the sqm calculations for you.

faqs.question: Do I need to include GST in my painting quote?
faqs.answer: Yes, if your business is registered for GST, your quote must clearly show the total price including GST. It's best practice to show a subtotal for labour and materials, the separate 10% GST amount, and the final inclusive total. This prevents confusion with the client and keeps you compliant with the ATO. Always label the final figure as 'Total Inc. GST'.

deck-quote-template.intro: This deck quote template is for carpenters building residential timber or composite decks. It suits everything from a small patio extension to a multi-level outdoor area. Most quotes go wrong on two fronts: underestimating the labour for digging footings, especially on rocky or sloping ground, and forgetting to factor in a 10-15% waste allowance for decking boards. Getting these details right protects your margin. Our template ensures all the critical line items are included, so you can build a professional quote that covers the full scope of the job.

sections.heading: How to Price Decking Materials and Labour
sections.body: Your biggest material cost is the decking itself. A standard 90mm Merbau board from a trade supplier is around $12 per lineal metre, so a 20 square metre deck needs about 238 lineal metres, costing roughly $2,850 plus GST before your markup. Don't forget the sub-frame; H3 treated pine for joists and bearers will add another $800-$1,000. Labour is the other major cost. A good starting point is to charge between $250 and $400 per square metre, including all labour from set-out to clean-up. A complex site with stairs or difficult access will be at the higher end of that range.

sections.heading: What Gets Left Off a Deck Building Quote
sections.body: It's the small things that eat your profit. Always include a line item for rubbish disposal; a 2 cubic metre skip bin costs around $300. Site access is another one. If you can't get a wheelbarrow to the deck area, you need to charge for carrying materials by hand. Also, check council requirements. Any deck over 1 metre from ground level, or of a certain size, may require a permit and engineering drawings, which is a cost you must pass on. Finally, specify the hardware. Using 316 marine grade stainless steel screws instead of galvanised can add hundreds to the job cost, so specify it clearly in the quote.

faqs.question: How much waste should I allow for on decking boards?
faqs.answer: For a standard rectangular deck using timber boards like Merbau, a 10% waste factor is usually safe. If you're using composite decking, which can be less forgiving, or laying boards in a herringbone pattern, increase that to 15%. It's cheaper to have a few boards left over than to make a special trip back to the supplier for a single length.

faqs.question: Does my deck quote need to mention Australian Standards?
faqs.answer: While you don't need to quote the whole rulebook, it’s good practice to state that the work will comply with the National Construction Code (NCC) and AS 1684 for timber framing. This shows the client you're a professional and protects you if they ask for something non-compliant. For balustrades, referencing AS 1170.1 for structural safety is key.

faqs.question: What's a fair price for concrete footings?
faqs.answer: Don't price footings per hole; price them based on total labour and materials. For a standard deck requiring twenty 400x400x600mm holes in stable soil, allow for a full day of labour for digging and pouring. With concrete mix and post supports, you should be quoting at least $1,200-$1,500 for the footings alone, before adding excavation machinery hire if needed.

fence-quote-template.intro: This fence quote template is for Australian fencers pricing typical residential jobs like Colorbond, timber paling, or aluminium slat fences. It’s set up to stop you losing money on the two things most guys get wrong: under-quoting labour for digging post holes in tough ground, and forgetting the cost of dumping the old fence. Get those right, and the rest of the job is pure profit. This guide gives you the numbers to plug into your template so you can quote accurately and move on.

sections.heading: How to Price Fence Installs Per Metre
sections.body: Most clients want a per-metre price. For a standard 1.8m Colorbond fence, this usually lands between $90 and $130 per linear metre. Labour is the biggest variable. Don't just charge a day rate. Price post hole digging separately, especially if it's rocky or clay soil, as that can double the time. A fair labour rate is around $80-$100 an hour. Factor in a 10% margin on materials from suppliers like Lysaght or your trade supplier. Using an app like QuoteMate helps pull real-time prices so you're not quoting off an old catalogue.

sections.heading: Line Items That Get Left Off a Fence Quote
sections.body: Forgetting site prep and disposal will kill your profit. Always include a line item for removing the old fence and another for tip fees, which can be $150+ per ute load. Is access tricky? If you’re carting materials up a steep driveway or through a house, add a labour charge for it. Council approval is another one. Most fences over 2 metres high need a permit, which is a cost you should pass on to the client. Finally, specify a provisional sum for hitting rock or pipes underground. It protects you from unexpected excavation costs.

faqs.question: How much waste factor should I add for timber palings?
faqs.answer: A safe bet is 10% for waste on timber palings to cover for splits, knots, and cutting to size. For a 20-metre fence, order 22 metres worth of timber. This buffer stops you from having to make a second trip to the supplier for just a few palings, saving you time and money. Always round up your material order.

faqs.question: How should I quote post holes for different soil types?
faqs.answer: Price per hole, not just as part of a day rate. For easy sandy soil, you might charge $25-$30 per hole. For heavy clay or rocky ground that needs a motorised auger, it should be closer to $50-$60 per hole plus any machine hire costs. This protects your margin if a 'quick job' turns into a full day of digging.

faqs.question: Does my quote need to reference an Australian Standard?
faqs.answer: For a standard boundary fence, you must follow local council rules on height and placement. However, if the fence is part of a pool barrier, you must build and quote it to meet AS 1926.1. Getting this wrong can mean having to tear it down at your own cost, so always check the specific pool safety rules first.

bathroom-renovation-quote-template.intro: This bathroom renovation quote template is for builders handling standard residential jobs, from a simple cosmetic update to a full gut-and-replace. Most quotes go wrong in two places: underestimating demolition labour and not pricing waterproofing to standard. Get those right, and you protect your margin. This template has the line items you need, from strip-out and waste disposal to the final coat of paint. It helps you build a detailed quote that covers every trade, fixture, and fitting, so you don't get caught out on costs halfway through the job.

sections.heading: Pricing the Big Three: Demolition, Waterproofing, and Tiling
sections.body: The bulk of your cost is in labour for demo, waterproofing, and tiling, not fancy taps. For a standard 3m x 2m bathroom, budget a full day for one labourer on demolition at around $400, plus another $400 for a skip bin. Waterproofing must meet AS 3740. A 15L pail of Davco K10 Plus from a trade supplier costs about $150 and covers the wet areas, but the real cost is the certified waterproofer's labour, easily $600-$800 including the certificate. For tiling, charge labour per square metre. Expect to pay $50-$70/m² for laying basic ceramics, and always add 15% to your tile order for cuts and waste.

sections.heading: What Gets Left Off a Bathroom Reno Quote
sections.body: Forgetting small items kills your profit. Did you check for asbestos? In an older home, testing and removal by a licensed specialist can add thousands and must be quoted separately. Factor in site access; a second-floor apartment with no lift means more labour time. Your quote should also flag potential variations like rotten floor joists found after demolition. And don't forget the sparky. Moving a GPO or adding an exhaust fan requires a licensed electrician, costing $500 or more and needing to comply with AS/NZS 3000. Using software like QuoteMate helps you build a checklist so these items are never missed.

faqs.question: How much should I add for contingency on a bathroom renovation?
faqs.answer: A 15-20% contingency is standard for bathroom renovations, especially on older properties. This covers unexpected issues like hidden water damage or old plumbing that needs replacing to meet current standards. Anything major, like finding asbestos, should be treated as a formal variation, not covered by the contingency. Be clear what your 15-20% covers.

faqs.question: Do I need to include a prime cost (PC) item for the tiles and tapware?
faqs.answer: Yes, using Prime Cost (PC) items for fixtures is best practice. It gives the client flexibility within a set budget. For example, specify a 'PC allowance of $55/m² for wall tiles' or '$400 for vanity tapware from Reece'. This protects you if the client chooses high-end fittings later. Your quote should still cover the fixed labour cost to install these items.

faqs.question: How long is a bathroom renovation quote usually valid for?
faqs.answer: Make your bathroom renovation quotes valid for 30 days. Supplier prices, especially for imported tiles and tapware, can change quickly. A 30-day validity protects you from having to absorb a price rise from a supplier like Tradelink or Beaumont Tiles. If a client accepts after this period, you have the right to re-price based on current costs.

pergola-quote-template.intro: This pergola quote template is for carpenters pricing standard residential jobs, from simple lean-tos to freestanding structures. Most quotes go wrong in two areas: underestimating labour for tricky sites and forgetting the waste factor on timber cuts. A good quote accounts for every hour and every offcut, not just the big-ticket items. This guide helps you price the job right, covering the real cost drivers and common omissions so your quote is accurate and you don't lose your margin on surprises that pop up mid-build.

sections.heading: How to Price Your Pergola Labour and Materials
sections.body: The biggest variables are timber choice and labour. A treated pine pergola might cost $150 per square metre in materials, while Merbau can easily push that to $300/sqm. Always check current lengths and prices at your timber yard or hardware supplier. For labour, don't just guess a day rate. Price it per task: 2 hours per footing, 4 hours for the main frame, 4 hours for roofing. Add a 10-15% waste factor on all timber lengths. A small 3x4m pergola is often a 2-day job for two carpenters, so factor in at least 32 hours of labour plus your margin and GST. Using quoting software like QuoteMate helps track these line items so nothing gets missed.

sections.heading: Costs Carpenters Forget on a Pergola Quote
sections.body: It's the small things that eat your profit. Did you include rubbish removal? A skip bin can be $300. What about spoil removal from digging footings? That's extra time and tip fees. Site access is a big one; if you can't get a ute near the site, you need to price in the labour to carry materials manually. Check if council approval is needed. This can add weeks of delay and cost over $500 in fees, which should be a separate line item. Finally, always include post stirrups and high-tensile bolts; they add up fast. For timber structures, referencing AS 1684 for span tables is a good way to justify your material choices.

faqs.question: How much more does a hardwood pergola cost than treated pine?
faqs.answer: Hardwoods like Merbau can cost two to three times more than H3 treated pine. For example, a 90x90mm Merbau post might be $50 per linear metre, while the equivalent treated pine post from a trade supplier is around $20. This price difference scales across the whole job, so confirm the client's budget and material choice before finalising the quote.

faqs.question: Should I quote for council approval fees?
faqs.answer: Yes, but list it as a separate provisional sum. Council application fees for a pergola can range from $200 to over $800 depending on your local council and the project value. By listing it separately, the client understands it's a direct cost you are managing on their behalf, not part of your building margin.

faqs.question: What's the best way to price concrete footings?
faqs.answer: Price footings per hole. A standard quote per footing might be $80-$120. This should cover labour to dig, one bag of Quick Set concrete from a supplier like CSR, the galvanised post stirrup, and cleanup. For hard or rocky ground that requires a jackhammer or special equipment, you need to add an extra labour charge per hour.

electrical-switchboard-upgrade-quote-tem.intro: This switchboard upgrade quote template is for sparkies doing residential upgrades, from replacing old ceramic fuse boxes to prepping for a solar install. Most quotes go wrong in two places: underestimating the time for mandatory testing and labelling of every circuit, and forgetting to factor in the cost of asbestos panel removal and disposal. A solid template stops you from quoting on guesswork and losing your margin. It makes sure every part, from the main switch to the compliance certificate, is on the invoice so you get paid for the whole job.

sections.heading: How to Price the Labour and Parts for a Standard Switchboard Swap
sections.body: The main cost is your time. A straight swap of a small board in an accessible spot takes 3-4 hours. At $95/hour, that's $285-$380 in labour. For materials, a standard 12-pole Clipsal Resi MAX enclosure from a wholesaler like TLE is about $90. Six RCBOs (combo RCD/MCB) at $40 each adds another $240. Add a main switch ($30) and sundries ($40). Your base cost is around $685 before GST and your margin. Using a tool like QuoteMate to pull real-time supplier pricing is crucial, as a 5% price jump on components can wipe out your profit on a small job.

sections.heading: What Sparkies Leave Off a Switchboard Quote
sections.body: The biggest miss is asbestos. If the board is mounted on an old fibro sheet, you must quote for specialist removal and disposal, which can be $500 or more. Don't touch it otherwise. Second is making good. If the new enclosure is smaller than the old one, you'll have wall patching and painting to do. Quote this as an optional extra or clearly exclude it. Finally, don't forget the Certificate of Electrical Safety (CES) lodgement fee, which varies by state but is your responsibility. This is a mandatory cost under the AS/NZS 3000 wiring rules and must be included.

faqs.question: How much should I allow for sundries on a switchboard quote?
faqs.answer: For a standard residential switchboard upgrade, a flat rate of $40-$60 for sundries is usually safe. This covers consumables like cable, conduit offcuts, neutral and earth bars, labels, and mounting screws. For larger or more complex commercial boards, calculating this as 5% of the total material cost is a better approach. Make sure your template lists this as a line item.

faqs.question: Do I need to quote for a new main switch?
faqs.answer: Yes, you must quote for replacing the main switch. Even if the old one seems to work, AS/NZS 3000 requires a main switch for effective isolation on all new installations and major alterations like a board upgrade. It's a critical safety component. A new 63A main switch from Clipsal costs about $30-$40 from most electrical wholesalers.

faqs.question: What if I find dodgy wiring during the upgrade?
faqs.answer: The quote must clearly define the scope. State that the price covers the switchboard replacement only. Include a clause that any pre-existing wiring faults discovered during mandatory testing will be documented and quoted as a separate variation. This protects you from fixing a house full of bad wiring for free. Your compliance testing is governed by AS/NZS 3000.

hot-water-system-replacement-quote-templ.intro: This is for plumbers quoting hot water system replacements. It covers like-for-like swaps of gas, electric, or heat pump units. The biggest mistakes plumbers make are under-quoting labour for difficult access and forgetting to price the disposal of the old unit. A good hot water system quote template accounts for the whole job, from draining the old tank to signing off the compliance certificate. Getting these details right at the start protects your margin and prevents arguments with the customer later on. It ensures you get paid for every part of the work.

sections.heading: How to Price a Straight Swap vs. an Upgrade
sections.body: A straight swap is the easiest. A 250L electric Rheem from Reece costs about $1300. Labour is 2-3 hours at your standard rate, say $120/hr. An upgrade from electric to gas continuous flow is more complex. The unit, like a Rinnai B26, is about $1600. Then you must add labour for running a new gas line, maybe $60 per metre, plus any new pipework. You might also need a sparkie to install a GPO. Using a quoting app like QuoteMate helps you add these separate line items so the customer sees the value and you don't forget the costs.

sections.heading: What Gets Left Off: Access, Disposal and Compliance Costs
sections.body: The unit's location changes the job completely. A system in a tight roof cavity or on a second-storey wall needs more labour than one in a garage. Add an hour or two for access. Getting rid of the old unit isn't free; most council tips charge $50-$100 for scrap metal disposal, plus your time to get it there. Every new installation requires a tempering valve to comply with AS/NZS 3500.4. This part is about $120 from Tradelink. Finally, include the cost of the compliance certificate required in your state. These small items add up.

faqs.question: Do I need to quote a tempering valve on every job?
faqs.answer: Yes, it’s mandatory under AS/NZS 3500.4 for all new storage hot water installations to prevent scalding. The valve limits water temperature at the tap to 50°C. Forgetting to quote this $120 part plus labour means you’re either non-compliant or doing the work for free. It’s a required line item.

faqs.question: How much should I charge for removing the old unit?
faqs.answer: Charge for your labour plus the tip fee. Labour is usually 30-45 minutes to drain, disconnect, and move the unit. Then add the disposal fee from your local council, which is often between $50 and $100. If it’s a heavy unit in a tricky spot, add extra labour for a two-person lift.

faqs.question: Is a heat pump much more expensive than a standard electric unit?
faqs.answer: Yes, the initial unit cost is higher. A standard 250L electric unit is about $1300, while a quality heat pump of a similar size from a supplier like Reece can be $3500-$4500. The plumbing is similar, but explain the long-term running cost savings to the customer. Factor in any government rebates that might apply.

solar-installation-quote-template.intro: This solar installation quote template is for residential jobs up to 10kW. It's built for Aussie solar installers quoting standard grid-connect systems. Most quotes go wrong in two places: under-pricing the labour on a steep or tricky roof, and miscalculating the STC rebate value on the day. Get those right, and you protect your margin. This template helps you list every component, from the panels down to the DC isolators, so you can price accurately and show the customer exactly what they're paying for before the rebate is applied.

sections.heading: Pricing Labour and Hardware for a Standard 6.6kW System
sections.body: A standard 6.6kW system has a pre-rebate base cost of around $5,500 to $8,000. This covers hardware and labour before your margin. Labour for two installers for a full day on a single-storey tin roof will be about $1,200 to $1,800. The hardware adds up: 16 x 415W panels from a supplier like One Stop Warehouse will be about $2,800. A 5kW Sungrow or Fronius string inverter adds another $1,200. Mounting gear from Clenergy might be $600. Add another $400 for cabling, conduit, and breakers from a wholesaler like TLE. The total pre-margin cost sits at a minimum of $6,200.

sections.heading: What Gets Left Off a Solar Quote: Access, Safety, and Switchboards
sections.body: The items that kill your profit are scaffold hire and switchboard upgrades. A steep tile roof (over 22 degrees) or any two-storey job requires edge protection under safety rules, adding $600 to $1,500 to your costs. If the customer's house has an old ceramic fuse board, it needs a full upgrade to comply with AS/NZS 3000, which can be another $1,000 to $2,000 surprise. Using a quoting app like QuoteMate lets you create saved line items for these extras so you can add them instantly. Always check the switchboard during the site visit. All solar work must follow AS/NZS 5033.

faqs.question: How do I calculate the STC rebate for my customer?
faqs.answer: Calculate STCs based on system size, location (zone), and the current year's deeming period. A 6.6kW system in Melbourne (Zone 4) creates fewer STCs than one in Brisbane (Zone 3). The STC price changes daily. Check a live trading site like Formbay for today's price, which usually sits between $38 and $40 per certificate.

faqs.question: Should I quote for a string inverter or microinverters?
faqs.answer: Quote microinverters for roofs with partial shading from trees or chimneys, or for customers wanting panel-level monitoring. They add around $2,000 to a 6.6kW system compared to a string inverter. For a simple, unshaded north-facing roof, a quality string inverter from a brand like Sungrow, sourced via a wholesaler like Middy's, is the most cost-effective option.

faqs.question: How does adding a battery change the quote?
faqs.answer: For battery storage, you must quote a hybrid inverter, not a standard solar inverter. A hybrid inverter like a Fronius Gen24 costs about $1,000 more than its solar-only equivalent. The battery itself, like a 10kWh Sungrow SBR, will add at least $7,000-$9,000 to the total quote, plus extra labour for installation and commissioning.

retaining-wall-quote-template.intro: This retaining wall quote template is for landscapers pricing jobs for residential or light commercial sites. It works for common timber sleeper, concrete sleeper, or block walls up to about 1.2 metres high. The biggest mistakes tradies make are under-quoting soil removal and forgetting to price proper drainage behind the wall. Get those two items right and the job stays profitable from the start. This retaining wall quote template helps you factor in every cost, so you can send the quote with confidence and protect your margin on the job.

sections.heading: Calculating Your Retaining Wall Costs per Metre
sections.body: A standard treated pine sleeper wall costs about $350-$450 per square metre. A concrete sleeper wall is closer to $500-$650 per square metre. These prices include materials and labour. Your material costs are straightforward: a 200x75mm treated pine sleeper from a trade supplier is about $30 for a 2.4m length, while galvanised steel H-posts are around $100 for a similar length. The real variable is labour. Budget for two labourers, as moving posts and sleepers is not a one-person job. Factor in at least 1.5 labour hours per lineal metre for a simple wall on a flat, accessible site. Add a 10% waste factor on materials and a separate line item for tip fees.

sections.heading: What Most Blokes Forget on a Retaining Wall Quote
sections.body: Site access and spoil removal are the two biggest costs left off quotes. If you can’t get a mini-digger in, you’re digging post holes by hand, which can double your labour time. Price that accordingly. Drainage is another one. Don't just quote for the ag pipe and gravel. You need to quote for the extra excavation to place it correctly, plus the geotextile fabric from a supplier like CSR to stop it from clogging. Finally, any wall over one metre high in most council areas needs engineering and a permit. This can add $1,500 to $2,500 to the job before you even break ground. All drainage should comply with AS 4678.

faqs.question: How much concrete do I need for retaining wall posts?
faqs.answer: A standard rule is one-third of the post length goes in the ground. For a 1.8m post holding a 1.2m wall, you'll have 600mm in the ground. A 300mm wide hole needs about two 20kg bags of concrete mix from a trade supplier per post. Always follow the engineer's specs if they are provided.

faqs.question: Do I need to charge for backfill material?
faqs.answer: Yes, unless the excavated soil is suitable, which it rarely is. Clean, free-draining backfill like sand or gravel is a material cost you must include. You'll need to quote for its supply and delivery from a local landscape supplier. Expect to pay around $70-$90 per cubic metre plus delivery fees.

faqs.question: When does a retaining wall need council approval?
faqs.answer: It varies by council, but a common trigger is any wall over one metre in height, or a wall built close to a property boundary. Always check the local council's development control plan online before finalising your quote. Quoting for a permit application and engineering drawings is a separate line item that can add thousands.

roof-restoration-quote-template.intro: This roof restoration quote template is for residential tile or metal roofs that need a full clean, repair, and repaint. It suits jobs from a 150 square metre single-storey home to a trickier two-storey place needing full edge protection. Most roofers get the price per square metre right for the membrane but lose money on the prep work. They either forget to factor in replacing more than a handful of broken tiles or underestimate the labour for a full repoint of the ridge caps. This template helps you price every step properly, from the pressure clean to the final coat.

sections.heading: Pricing Your Materials and Labour Per Square Metre
sections.body: Your base rate is square metres. A typical 3-bedroom home is 180-220m². Price your membrane per square metre. A 15L drum of Dulux AcraTex Roof Membrane from a trade supplier costs around $260 and covers about 40m² for two coats. That's $6.50/m² just for the paint. Factor in sealer at around $2/m². Labour is your big variable. A straightforward single-storey tile roof might take two guys two days, so 32 hours total. At $75/hour per man, that's $2,400 in labour before materials or overheads. Always add a 10-15% waste factor on your membrane for steeply pitched roofs.

sections.heading: What Most Roofers Forget to Add to the Quote
sections.body: Safety rail hire is the biggest forgotten cost. For a two-storey job, SafeWork requires edge protection, which can add $1,500-$3,000 to the price from a local hire company. Another is waste disposal. A full repoint means chipping off old mortar, creating kilograms of rubble. You'll need to price in a small skip bin or tip fees. Also, don't just quote for a few broken tiles; get on the roof and check properly. Using quoting software like QuoteMate helps you build a library of these optional line items, so you never forget to add scaffold hire or extra tile costs again. Always check the sarking condition where visible.

faqs.question: How much extra should I quote for a terracotta roof vs a concrete tile roof?
faqs.answer: Terracotta tiles are more brittle and often require a more specialised sealer. Add 10-15% to your labour for the extra care needed during pressure cleaning to avoid breakage. The sealer itself, like CSR Monier's Terracotta Glaze, can also be more expensive than a standard primer, so check current pricing with your supplier before finalising the quote.

faqs.question: Do I need to quote for replacing all the ridge cap pointing?
faqs.answer: If more than a third of the pointing is cracked or loose, it's faster and gives a better result to quote for a full repoint. A partial job often fails within a few years. A full repoint on a standard roof uses about four to five 10kg bags of flexible pointing mortar, like Shieldcoat's Shieldflex, which costs around $40 per bag.

faqs.question: What's the standard warranty to offer on a roof restoration?
faqs.answer: Most professional roof coatings come with a manufacturer's warranty of 10-15 years. You should offer a warranty that matches the product you're using. For example, Dulux AcraTex offers a 15-year warranty when applied by a registered applicator according to their specifications. Always provide this in writing, as it protects both you and the homeowner.

granny-flat-quote-template.intro: This granny flat quote template is for builders quoting new-builds up to 60m² in Australia. It covers standard slab-on-ground, timber or steel frame construction. The biggest mistakes we see are underquoting site preparation and forgetting council fees. A patch of grass looks cheap to build on until you hit rock or need to run services 50 metres from the main house. Using a granny flat quote template in an app like QuoteMate helps you track every variable, from excavation to the final private certifier inspection, ensuring your price is right.

sections.heading: How to Price the Core Structure of a Granny Flat
sections.body: Your profit is made or lost on the big three: slab, frame, and roof. Price concrete per square metre, not just per cubic metre. A 60m² slab can cost $15,000-$20,000 ($250-$330/m²) including formwork, mesh, and labour. For framing, price MGP10 pine per lineal metre, currently around $7/m at trade rates, and add a 15% waste factor. Roofs are priced per square metre; expect to pay about $60-$80/m² for a standard Colorbond roof, supplied and installed. Labour on a typical frame and roof package will run you about $15,000-$25,000 depending on complexity.

sections.heading: Forgetting These Items Will Cost You on a Granny Flat Build
sections.body: It's the small things that add up. Site access is a big one; if you can’t get a standard truck in, you’ll need to budget for a mini-excavator at $500/day plus operator. Soil and rubbish removal requires skip bins, costing $400-$800 each. Don't forget statutory costs. Council DA or CDC application fees, private certifier stage inspections, and mandatory termite management (as per AS 3660.1) can easily add $10,000 to the job before you've even broken ground. These are real costs, not optional extras. Include them as separate line items so the client sees the value.

faqs.question: How much should I allow for council and utility connection fees?
faqs.answer: This varies by council. Budget $5,000-$10,000 for standard fees, certifiers, and inspections. Water, sewer, and electricity connections can add another $5,000-$15,000 depending on the site's distance from the mains. Always get a specific written quote from the local utility providers before you finalise your price for the client.

faqs.question: What's a realistic contingency to add to a 60m² granny flat quote?
faqs.answer: For a standard 60m² build on a level block, a 10% contingency is the minimum for material price shifts and small client changes. If it's a tricky site with poor access or a steep slope, push that up to 15-20%. Anything less than 10% is asking for trouble on a fixed-price contract.

faqs.question: Do I need to quote for termite management?
faqs.answer: Yes, it's mandatory under the National Construction Code and AS 3660.1. You must include a termite management system. This could be a physical barrier installed during the slab pour or a chemical reticulation system. Forgetting this will fail your inspection and can cost you thousands to fix later.

split-system-installation-quote-template.intro: This split system installation quote template is for standard back-to-back domestic jobs. It helps you price the install of single-head units up to about 7kW. Most tradies get burned on quoting these by underestimating labour for tricky pipe runs or completely forgetting to price a new dedicated electrical circuit from the switchboard. They’ll quote for a simple install and end up doing a complex one for the same money. This template makes sure you account for the real costs, protecting your margin on every job.

sections.heading: How to Price a Standard Back-to-Back Install
sections.body: A standard 2.5kW back-to-back install is your baseline. The unit itself, say a Mitsubishi from The Good Guys Trade, will be $800-$1100. Add materials: a wall bracket ($50 from a trade supplier), 3 metres of copper pair coil from Reece ($60-$90), and an electrical isolator ($30). Labour is the biggest variable. A straightforward job takes 3-4 hours for one tech. At $100/hour, that's $300-$400. So, your base cost before markup and GST is around $1240-$1670. Always add a small percentage for consumables like fixings and sealant. Check your supplier for current unit pricing before every quote.

sections.heading: Forgetting These Items Will Cost You Money
sections.body: The profit disappears in the extras. Did you quote for a new circuit? A dedicated run from the switchboard can add $400-$600 in labour and materials. Is the wall double brick or concrete? Core drilling adds an hour of labour plus tool wear. Access is another one; quoting a job that needs a scissor lift and not including the hire fee is a classic mistake. Using a quoting app like QuoteMate lets you build a library of these add-on items, so you never forget to include them. Finally, all electrical work must comply with AS/NZS 3000, so factor in time for correct installation.

faqs.question: How much extra should I quote for a non-standard pipe run?
faqs.answer: For runs beyond the standard 3 metres, charge per metre. A good rule of thumb is $50-$70 per additional metre. This covers the extra copper from a supplier like Reece, the pipe capping, fixings, and your labour. For a tricky 'up-and-over' through the roof space, add at least two hours to your labour estimate.

faqs.question: Do I need to include disposal of the old air con unit?
faqs.answer: Yes, always add a line item for it. Degassing and removing an old unit can take 30-60 minutes. On top of that, you have the cost of legally disposing of it at a waste transfer station, which can be around $30-$50 depending on your local council. Forgetting this item means you’re paying to get rid of their rubbish.

faqs.question: What's the difference in quoting for a 2.5kW vs a 7.1kW unit?
faqs.answer: The unit cost is the main difference; a 7.1kW unit can be double the price of a 2.5kW. The larger unit also requires heavier gauge electrical cable and potentially a larger circuit breaker, adding to material costs. Labour is similar for a back-to-back install, but bigger units are heavier, so you might need two techs for the lift.

end-of-lease-cleaning-quote-template.intro: This end of lease cleaning quote template is for professional cleaners quoting residential jobs in Australia. It’s built for anything from a one-bedroom apartment to a four-bedroom house. Most cleaners get stung in two places: underestimating the time for a proper oven deep clean, and not being specific about what their ‘bond-back guarantee’ covers. This template helps you price correctly so you don't end up working for free fixing issues that weren't your fault. Get the details right and avoid arguments with property managers.

sections.heading: How to Price an End of Lease Clean
sections.body: Your biggest cost is labour. Charge a flat rate based on the property size, not by the hour. A typical 2-bedroom, 1-bathroom unit takes two cleaners 4-5 hours, so base your price on 8-10 total labour hours. At $50/hour, that’s $400-$500 in labour. Add costs for specialised gear like a commercial carpet steamer, which might add $80-$120 to the job. Factor in about $30-$50 for consumables like oven degreaser and window cleaner from a trade supplier. Always add a ‘heavy soil’ clause for properties left in a bad state. For a standard 2-bed unit, you should be quoting around $550-$700 including GST.

sections.heading: What Gets Left Off a Bond Cleaning Quote
sections.body: The agent's checklist is long, so it's easy to miss things. Garages, balconies, and exterior window tracks are classic examples. Inside, cleaning air conditioner filters and exhaust fan covers is often forgotten but always checked. Wall washing is another big one; your quote should specify spot cleaning of marks only, with a full wall wash priced as a separate line item. Always include a charge for parking if it’s a city job. Finally, state that your quote does not cover rubbish removal for items left by the tenant. The job is to clean an empty property, not to do a tip run.

faqs.question: Do I need to charge extra for heavy carpet stains?
faqs.answer: Yes. Your standard steam clean price covers general dirt. Quote separately for treating significant stains like red wine or pet urine. These need specific chemicals and more labour. List this as a provisional cost on the quote, so the client knows it's extra before you start. This protects you from losing money on a tough job.

faqs.question: What does a 'bond-back guarantee' actually cover?
faqs.answer: It means you will return, free of charge, to fix any cleaning issues noted on the property manager’s exit report that relate to your service checklist. It's not a money-back offer. The guarantee should be valid for a set time, usually 48-72 hours after the clean. It doesn't cover new mess or damage made after you leave.

faqs.question: Should I charge a fixed price or by the hour?
faqs.answer: Always quote a fixed price. It gives the client certainty and stops them watching the clock. Figure out your total estimated hours, multiply by your rate ($45-$65/hr), then add materials and a 15% margin for tricky spots. A quoting tool like QuoteMate helps you build these line items into a professional fixed-price quote that protects your profit.

pool-fencing-quote-template.intro: This pool fencing quote template is for fencers and builders pricing residential jobs in Australia. It suits standard glass or aluminium fencing installations. Most quotes go wrong on two items: underestimating the labour for core drilling into concrete, and completely forgetting to add the cost of the final compliance certificate. Getting these right protects your profit margin on the whole job. Use this template to make sure your numbers are accurate and every cost is covered before you send the quote to the client.

sections.heading: Pricing Panels and Labour Per Metre
sections.body: Frameless glass is a premium product, costing $250-$350 per linear metre for materials alone. A 1.2m panel from a supplier like Glass Outlet costs about $150, plus two stainless steel spigots at $40 each. Aluminium is far cheaper, around $80-$120 per metre in materials from a trade supplier. Labour is the other big factor. Glass needs two people to lift safely, so budget for two installers at $80-$110 per hour each. A standard 20-metre job can take a full day. Aluminium can be a one-person job. Always add a 5% waste factor for panel offcuts or breakage.

sections.heading: What Tradies Forget on a Pool Fencing Quote
sections.body: The small things sink your profit. First, site access. If you can't get the ute close, add labour for carrying heavy glass panels through a house. Second, core drilling. It’s slow work. A diamond core drill bit wears out, and hiring one costs over $100 a day. Price each core hole as a separate labour task. Finally, include the certifier's fee of $400-$600. Using a tool like QuoteMate helps you build a library of these easily forgotten items so they appear on every quote. Always specify that the installation will meet the AS 1926.1 standard.

faqs.question: How much should I add for a compliant gate?
faqs.answer: A compliant pool gate needs self-closing hinges and a self-latching mechanism. A full kit from a supplier like D&D Technologies with a MagnaLatch and TruClose hinges will cost between $150 and $300 in materials alone. Don't just price a standard hinge; list the specific compliant hardware on your quote.

faqs.question: Do I charge more for a sloping block?
faqs.answer: Yes. A sloping site means stepping the panels, which requires longer posts and more time to get levels right. You can't just run the fence parallel to the ground. Add at least 15-20% to your labour cost for a moderate slope, as it adds a couple of hours to a standard job.

faqs.question: Who pays for the final compliance certificate?
faqs.answer: The client pays, but you must include it on your quote. As the installer, you are responsible for arranging the inspection. Include the private certifier's fee, usually $400-$600, as a separate line item. This confirms the job will be done to Australian Standard AS 1926.1.

staircase-quote-template.intro: This staircase quote template is for carpenters building internal timber stairs for new builds or renovations. It works for straight flights, quarter-turn, and half-turn stairs. Most quotes go wrong in two places: under-pricing the labour for complex balustrades and forgetting the cost of site prep and temporary access during the build. Getting these details right at the start keeps your profit margin safe. Use this guide to make sure your numbers are accurate and you’ve covered every line item before you send the quote to the builder or homeowner.

sections.heading: How to Price Stair Materials and Labour
sections.body: Your main costs are stringers, treads, and the balustrade. A standard pair of pre-primed pine stringers for a 2.7m ceiling might cost $300 from a trade supplier. Victorian Ash or Merbau will be double that. Price treads individually; a standard 900mm Tassie Oak tread is about $60. Labour is the biggest variable. A simple, straight flight might take two carpenters 1.5 days (24 hours total). A winder staircase with a glass balustrade could take 4-5 days. Always factor labour at your hourly rate, say $85/hr, plus 15% for material waste and fixings. QuoteMate can store these rates to make pricing consistent.

sections.heading: What Gets Left Off a Staircase Quote
sections.body: It's easy to miss the non-obvious costs. Site access can be a big one; if you need to hire a small crane or scaffold to get stringers to a second floor, add that cost. Demolition and disposal of an old staircase can add half a day's labour plus tip fees. Also, check if structural changes are needed to the floor joists to create the stair void. This requires engineering sign-off, which is a separate cost. Finally, all stairs and balustrades must comply with the National Construction Code (NCC) Part 3.9.1 for dimensions and safety, so make sure your design is compliant before you price it.

faqs.question: How much extra should I quote for a glass balustrade?
faqs.answer: A glass balustrade is a specialist job. Instead of timber balusters at $15 each, you're looking at toughened glass panels that cost $300-$500 per linear metre supplied and installed. This includes the stainless steel spigots or channel fixings. Always get a direct quote from a glass supplier and add your margin, don't guess the price.

faqs.question: Do I need to include temporary handrails in my quote?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the site will be active while you work. WorkSafe rules require fall protection. A temporary handrail is your responsibility until the permanent balustrade is installed. You can build a simple one with construction pine and charge for 2-3 hours of labour plus materials, or hire a temporary edge protection system for around $40 per metre per week.

faqs.question: What's the Australian standard for riser and tread dimensions?
faqs.answer: The National Construction Code (NCC) dictates the dimensions. The riser height must be between 115mm and 190mm. The tread depth (going) must be between 240mm and 355mm. The slope relationship (2 x Riser + 1 x Going) must fall between 550mm and 700mm. These dimensions are detailed in NCC 2022 Volume Two, Part 3.9.1.

termite-treatment-quote-template.intro: This termite treatment quote template is for residential and light commercial jobs, covering both chemical barriers and baiting systems. Quoting termite work goes wrong in two main areas: underestimating the chemical volume needed for the soil type and forgetting to price difficult access like drilling through tiled patios or concrete paths. Get those two things right and your margin is protected. A solid template stops you from guessing and ensures every litre of termiticide and every hour of labour is accounted for, giving the customer a clear price and you a profitable job.

sections.heading: How to Price a Chemical Barrier per Lineal Metre
sections.body: Your main cost is the chemical. A 2.5L bottle of Termidor SC from a supplier like Garrards costs around $550 and makes up to 416L of solution. For a standard trench and treat, you’ll use about 10L of mixed solution per lineal metre. That’s a chemical cost of about $13.20 per metre. Labour is next. A two-man team at $80/hr each takes time to trench, mix, and apply. Factor in at least 15 minutes of labour per metre, which adds another $40. Add costs for drilling concrete, plus your equipment wear and margin. A starting price of $65-$85 per lineal metre is a safe baseline before site-specific extras.

sections.heading: The Real Costs Left Off Most Termite Quotes
sections.body: Forgetting site prep and reinstatement will kill your profit. Drilling through concrete paths or tiled areas requires not just the bit, but the time and cost to patch the holes cleanly. Quote this as a separate line item, around $25-$40 per lineal metre. If you hit rocks and need a jackhammer, that's extra labour. Also, factor in the cost of removing and disposing of old or contaminated soil if required. Finally, always include the annual inspection plan as a separate, optional item on the quote. The work must comply with Australian Standard AS 3660, so your Certificate of Treatment has to be included in the price.

faqs.question: How do I quote a baiting system versus a chemical barrier?
faqs.answer: A chemical barrier has a high upfront cost for chemical and labour but lower ongoing fees. A baiting system has a lower initial installation cost but requires a mandatory, higher-priced annual monitoring program. Present both options clearly. The baiting system quote must always include the first year's monitoring contract, as per the chemical manufacturer's warranty requirements.

faqs.question: What's a fair price to add for drilling through a concrete path?
faqs.answer: Charge this per lineal metre, not per hour. It covers the specialised drill bits, labour, and patching material. A fair rate is between $25 and $40 per metre on top of your standard treatment cost. For thicker, reinforced concrete, you should be charging at the higher end of that range. Don't forget to check for pipes before you start drilling.

faqs.question: Should the annual inspection be included in the main treatment price?
faqs.answer: No, quote it separately. The main quote is for the active treatment and installation. The annual inspection is a separate service to maintain the warranty and check for new activity. List it as an optional line item for around $280-$450 per year, depending on the property size. This makes your upfront price clearer and sets up recurring revenue.

gutter-replacement-quote-template.intro: This gutter replacement quote template is for standard residential jobs, single or double storey. Most roofers get the per-metre price right but lose money on waste factors and disposal costs. Underestimating cuts on a complex roofline or the tip fees for old steel gutters can wipe out your profit before you start. This template helps you price every part of the job properly, from new downpipes to the final site clean-up. It's built to make sure you get paid for every bracket, rivet, and hour you're on the tools, so you don't end up working for free.

sections.heading: How to price the real costs of a gutter job
sections.body: Your main costs are materials and labour. Price Colorbond quad gutter from a supplier like Lysaght or Stratco at around $12-$18 per lineal metre, but always add a 15% waste factor for cuts and corners. Labour is where quotes vary. For a straightforward single-storey house, you might charge $60-$80 per lineal metre for removal and installation. For a two-storey house with difficult access, that can jump to $100-$140 per metre. Don't forget sundries like silicone, rivets, and brackets—allow about 5% of the total material cost. A quoting app like QuoteMate helps you save these as standard line items so they're never forgotten.

sections.heading: What most roofers leave off a gutter quote
sections.body: Forgetting access equipment and correct disposal will destroy your margin. A single-storey job might just need ladders, but anything over 3 metres or on a steep pitch requires edge protection or scaffolding. This can add $600-$2000+ to the job cost. Also, budget for waste disposal. A ute-load of old steel guttering might cost $150 at the tip. If you find old asbestos gutters, you need a licensed remover, which can add thousands. Always check the fascia boards for rot. Replacing a few metres of timber fascia can add another $400 in materials and labour. All installations must comply with AS/NZS 3500.3 for roof drainage.

faqs.question: How much waste should I actually factor in for guttering?
faqs.answer: For a simple rectangular roof, a 10% waste factor is usually safe. For a complex roof with multiple hips, valleys, and corners, you need to increase that to 15-20%. It's always cheaper to have a half-length of gutter left over than it is to send an apprentice back to a supplier like Stratco for a single piece, losing hours of paid labour.

faqs.question: Should I quote for replacing fascia boards as well?
faqs.answer: Always inspect the fascia while you're measuring up. If you see peeling paint, soft spots, or water stains, quote to replace those sections as an optional extra for the client. It is much better to price the potential variation upfront than to argue about it halfway through the job. A standard 4.2m length of primed timber fascia costs around $40 from a trade supplier.

faqs.question: Is it worth quoting for leaf guards?
faqs.answer: Always offer leaf guard as a separate, optional line item. Explain the benefit, especially if there are overhanging trees, but make it clear it's an add-on as it can significantly increase labour time. A good quality aluminium gutter mesh can add $30-$50 per metre to the final price, so it's a profitable upsell if the customer wants it.

colorbond-fence-quote-template.intro: This Colorbond fence quote template is for fencers on residential and light commercial jobs. It covers standard installations on level or slightly sloping ground. The biggest mistakes tradies make when quoting Colorbond are underestimating labour on uneven ground and forgetting the cost of removing and dumping the old fence. A good quote accounts for every post hole, every bag of concrete, and the time it takes to clear the site before you even start. Get those details right and you protect your profit margin on the whole job.

sections.heading: How to price your labour and materials per metre
sections.body: Your price should be built per linear metre. For a standard 1.8m high fence, materials from a trade supplier or a local steel merchant will be about $90-$110 per metre. This includes the panel, rails, posts, caps, and concrete. Don't forget screws and brackets. Labour is the key variable. On a clear, level site, budget for 1-1.5 hours per panel for two people. That's digging, setting posts, and attaching sheets. At $70/hr per person, that's roughly $140-$210 in labour per 2.35m panel. Always add a 10% contingency for material waste, especially on runs that aren't a perfect multiple of the panel length.

sections.heading: What gets left off a Colorbond fence quote
sections.body: Forgetting site prep and disposal will kill your profit. Is there an old timber or asbestos fence to remove? A 4 cubic metre skip bin for timber costs around $350-$450. Asbestos removal requires a specialist and costs thousands. What about access? If you can't get a mini-digger in, you're digging post holes by hand, which doubles your labour time. Check for underground services using Dial Before You Dig. Also, any fence over 2 metres high may need a council permit, which is a cost you should pass on to the client. The steel itself should conform to Australian Standard AS 1397 for coating and durability.

faqs.question: How much extra should I charge for a sloping block?
faqs.answer: For a gentle slope, add 15-20% to your labour for raking the panels. A steep site that needs to be stepped can double your labour per section due to extra cutting and the need for longer posts. You must quote for the extra post length and concrete for each step. Don't absorb this cost – spell it out as a line item.

faqs.question: What's the right amount of concrete for fence posts?
faqs.answer: Use a 20MPa mix. For a standard post in a 600mm deep hole, one 20kg bag of quick-set concrete from a trade supplier is usually enough. For gate posts or corner posts in high-wind areas, use two bags per hole to be safe. Your quote should specify the number of bags you're using so the client sees the value.

faqs.question: Do I need to include GST on my Colorbond quote?
faqs.answer: Yes, if your business is registered for GST, your quote must show the 10% tax. The final price you present to the customer must be the total amount including GST. Using a quoting app like QuoteMate adds the GST automatically and displays it correctly on the PDF, so you don't have to worry about the calculation or confusing the client.

shower-screen-quote-template.intro: This shower screen quote template is for glaziers pricing standard installs in residential bathrooms. It covers frameless, semi-frameless, and framed screens up to 2.1 metres high. The biggest mistakes are underquoting labour for out-of-square walls and forgetting the cost of high-quality silicone. A cheap sealant fails in two years and costs you a callback, wrecking your profit. Get the labour and consumables right, and the glass price is easy to manage. This template helps you remember every line item for a profitable job, so you can send a professional shower screen quote every time.

sections.heading: How to Price Labour and Hardware Correctly
sections.body: A standard frameless screen takes two people about 2-3 hours, so budget $200-$300 for labour. Add an extra hour if the walls are badly out of plumb and need custom channels or packers. Hardware is the next variable. A set of basic chrome hinges and a handle from Reece might run you $150, but a matte black or brushed brass finish can easily double that. Always check current supplier pricing. Don't forget consumables. A good quality sanitary-grade silicone from a trade supplier for around $25 a tube is essential. It's the difference between a clean, long-lasting finish and a mouldy callback. Factor in at least half a tube per screen.

sections.heading: What Glaziers Forget to Add to the Quote
sections.body: Forgetting disposal of the old screen is a classic mistake. A trip to the tip can cost $50-$80 in fees and eats up your time. Always add a line item for removal and disposal. Also, check site access. Are you carrying a 2-metre glass panel up three flights of stairs? That’s extra time and risk, so add a site access or difficult access fee. Finally, all safety glass installations must comply with AS 1288. This dictates minimum thickness and fixing requirements. You don't quote the standard itself, but complying might mean using thicker, more expensive glass, especially for larger panels. Check the glass span tables in AS 1288 before finalising your price.

faqs.question: How much extra should I charge for matte black hardware?
faqs.answer: Matte black, brushed nickel, or brass hardware can be 50-100% more expensive than standard polished chrome. Check the latest catalogue from your supplier like Tradelink or Reece before quoting. A chrome hinge set might be $80, while the same thing in matte black could be $160 or more. Always confirm the exact price before sending the quote.

faqs.question: What's the Australian Standard for shower screens?
faqs.answer: The key standard is AS 1288: Glass in buildings – Selection and installation. It specifies the type and thickness of safety glass required for bathrooms to prevent serious injury. For frameless screens, this usually means using toughened Grade A safety glass, typically 10mm thick, to meet the standard's requirements for human impact safety.

faqs.question: Should I quote for waterproofing repairs?
faqs.answer: Only if you are licensed to do so. If you remove an old framed screen and see damage to the waterproof membrane, you must stop. Inform the client they need a licensed waterproofer to repair it to AS 3740 standards before you can proceed. You can quote for the screen install, conditional on the substrate being sound and ready.

led-downlight-installation-quote-templat.intro: This LED downlight installation quote template is for Australian sparkies doing residential jobs, from a single-room swap-out to a full new-build fit-out. Most quotes go wrong in two places: underestimating labour for tricky ceiling access and forgetting to price quality, compatible dimmer switches. This leads to blown budgets and callbacks. Our template includes the specific line items you need to cover materials, labour, compliance, and access so you can price the job right the first time and protect your margin. Get it right and the job is profitable and straightforward.

sections.heading: How to Price the Labour and Materials for an LED Install
sections.body: Your labour is the biggest cost. A standard install into plasterboard with good roof space access takes 30-45 minutes per light. A tricky job with old wiring or limited access can push that to an hour or more. For materials, a decent 9W tri-colour dimmable LED from Beacon Lighting might be $20-$30 trade price. A compatible Clipsal trailing-edge dimmer switch is another $50-$70. Don't forget the 1.5mm TPS cable at roughly $1.50 a metre from your wholesaler, plus a few bucks per light for connectors and consumables. Always check current trade pricing before finalising the quote.

sections.heading: What Sparkies Leave Off an LED Downlight Quote
sections.body: Forgetting the Certificate of Electrical Safety is a common mistake. It's a required sign-off and takes time to complete and file. Also, what happens if you hit a ceiling joist? Quoting for 'minor patching' as a provisional sum covers you. If the client has old halogen transformers, you need to quote for their removal and disposal. Every installation must comply with AS/NZS 3000, particularly the rules around clearances for insulation around IC-rated downlights. Always add a line item for testing, including insulation resistance and polarity checks, before you hand the job over. This ensures compliance and safety.

faqs.question: How much labour time should I quote per downlight?
faqs.answer: For a standard install with easy access, budget 30-45 minutes per light at your hourly rate. If you're crawling through a tight roof space or fishing cables down a wall, charge for at least 60-90 minutes per light. Always price the first light higher to cover your site setup and pack-down time.

faqs.question: Do I need to specify the dimmer type on the quote?
faqs.answer: Yes, always. Specify a 'trailing-edge' or 'universal' dimmer compatible with LEDs to avoid callbacks for flickering or buzzing. Cheaper leading-edge dimmers won't work properly. A quality Clipsal or Legrand dimmer costs more, so listing the model on your quote justifies the price to the customer.

faqs.question: What's the general rule for spacing downlights?
faqs.answer: For a standard 2.4m ceiling, space 9W downlights about 1.5 to 2 metres apart. Place the first row about half that distance (75cm-1m) from the wall to light the room's edges. This is a rule of thumb, so always confirm the final layout with the client before you start drilling holes.

epoxy-floor-coating-quote-template.intro: This epoxy floor coating quote template is for flooring installers pricing up residential garages, workshops, or small commercial spaces. Using quoting software like QuoteMate helps you build these items in, but the initial numbers have to be right. Most tradies get tripped up on two things: underestimating the cost of diamond grinding the slab, and not testing for moisture. A wet slab will cause the coating to fail, and a poorly prepped surface guarantees a callback. This template helps you price the prep correctly so you can submit a quote that protects your profit.

sections.heading: How to Price Per Square Metre for Epoxy
sections.body: Price epoxy floors per square metre (m²). A simple two-coat garage floor might be $35-$50/m², while a decorative flake floor for a commercial site could be $100+/m². Your biggest variable is surface preparation. Diamond grinding a soft slab might be $10/m², but hard, cured concrete could be double that. Your material cost for a standard two-coat system from a supplier like On-Crete or All Purpose Coatings will run about $15-$25/m². Always add a 10-15% waste factor. Labour is at least two site visits, so price that accordingly. A 100m² job is easily $5,000 before labour.

sections.heading: Line Items That Get Left Off an Epoxy Quote
sections.body: Forgetting small items kills your profit on an epoxy job. Always test for concrete moisture. If it's high, you need a moisture barrier primer, which adds another $10-$15/m² in material costs. Quote for crack and joint repairs as a separate line item, either per linear metre or as a fixed sum. Filling a saw cut is not the same as a light skim coat. If the client wants coving up the walls, price that per linear metre as it's labour-intensive. Finally, add a line for waste disposal. A concrete grinder and dust extractor will fill multiple bags, and you have to pay to dump that. This is crucial for jobs that must meet AS 4586 slip resistance standards.

faqs.question: How much extra should I quote for a decorative flake floor system?
faqs.answer: A flake system adds significant material and labour. You're adding the cost of the vinyl flakes plus at least one extra clear polyurethane topcoat to encapsulate them. You should factor in an additional $20-$40 per square metre on top of your standard two-coat epoxy price. Check current flake prices from your supplier like Designer Flake before finalising the quote.

faqs.question: What's the best way to quote for fixing a badly damaged slab?
faqs.answer: Quote major repairs separately from the coating itself. Price concrete patching or self-levelling compounds per bag plus labour. For deep cracks or spalls, quote a per-linear-metre rate for grinding out and filling with an epoxy mortar. This isolates the risk if the repair work is worse than it looks. A 20kg bag of Ardex K 15 leveller covers about 4m² at 3mm thickness.

faqs.question: Do I need to put curing times on my quote?
faqs.answer: Yes, always specify the curing timeline. A standard epoxy system needs 24 hours before light foot traffic and up to 7 days for a full chemical cure to withstand vehicle traffic and spills. Stating this clearly on the quote manages the client's expectations about when they can use the space and prevents arguments later. This is non-negotiable for commercial jobs with tight schedules.

driveway-gate-quote-template.intro: This driveway gate quote template is for welders and fabricators pricing residential and light commercial jobs. It suits everything from a simple manual swing gate to a fully automated sliding one. Most quotes go wrong on two things: underestimating the labour for site prep and installation, and forgetting the cost of the electrical hook-up for the motor. Using a tool like our QuoteMate app helps you build a quote that covers every part of the job, from the steel to the final coat of paint, so you don't lose your margin on forgotten items.

sections.heading: How to Price Gate Fabrication and Labour
sections.body: Steel and aluminium prices change constantly. Price your frame and infill per linear metre, adding a 15% waste factor for offcuts. For a standard 3.5-metre sliding gate, budget around 8-10 hours of workshop fabrication time at your going rate, say $90/hour plus GST. Site installation is a separate beast. A simple post-and-swing install might take 4-6 hours, but a sliding gate with track, motor, and sensors can easily take a full day. Always factor in a separate line item for concrete for the post footings, typically 3-4 bags of general purpose mix from a trade supplier per post.

sections.heading: What Most Welders Forget on Driveway Gate Quotes
sections.body: It’s the small stuff that kills your margin. Did you quote for digging the post holes or trenching for the 240V cable? That's a half-day of labour plus equipment hire. What about rubbish removal for the old gate or soil from the dig? Add a line item for a tip run. If the site has tight access, you might need to price in extra labour for carrying materials. For automated gates, safety is critical. You must include photo-electric safety beams and ensure the motor has obstruction detection. Forgetting these items can cost you hundreds and leave you liable on site.

faqs.question: How much should I budget for powder coating?
faqs.answer: Powder coating is done by specialists, so quote it as a subcontracted cost. A standard 3.5m x 1.8m gate will cost between $350 and $550 depending on the colour and finish. Always get a current price from your local powder coater before finalising your quote. Reputable brands like Dulux or Interpon offer a wide range of durable finishes.

faqs.question: Do I need to quote for an electrician for a gate motor?
faqs.answer: Yes, absolutely. A gate motor requires a 240V weatherproof GPO installed by a licensed electrician. You should include this as a provisional sum from a sparky you work with. The work must comply with AS/NZS 3000, so don't do it yourself. A typical GPO install for a gate costs between $400 and $700.

faqs.question: What contingency should I add for a sloping driveway?
faqs.answer: A sloping site adds significant complexity. A sliding gate will need a custom-raked bottom rail to match the slope, and a swing gate may require specialised rising hinges. Add a minimum of 25% to your fabrication and installation labour estimates to account for the extra cutting, welding, and setup time. Don't price it like a flat-ground job.

tree-removal-quote-template.intro: This tree removal quote template is for Australian arborists pricing residential and commercial jobs. It suits everything from a single backyard gum tree to a multi-tree site clearance. The two things most often underquoted are stump grinding depth and green waste disposal. A shallow grind leaves a hump the mower will hit, and underestimating the weight of a hardwood log can kill your margin at the tip. Get those two right and the rest of the job will stack up properly.

sections.heading: How to Price Labour, Equipment, and Waste on a Tree Job
sections.body: Your price is built from labour, gear, and disposal. A climbing arborist might be on $600-$800 a day, with a groundie on $400. Factor in equipment wear and running costs. A decent chipper from Kennards Hire is $400-$500 a day. Chainsaw chains, fuel, and oil add up. Finally, green waste disposal is a big one. Council tip fees vary but expect to pay $80-$150 per tonne. A mature gum tree can easily be a few tonnes, so don't guess. The most accurate way is to use a public weighbridge on your first run to the tip.

sections.heading: Costs Arborists Forget to Include on Quotes
sections.body: Access is a major cost driver often missed. If you can’t get the chipper to the tree, you’re dragging branches by hand, which adds hours. Overhead powerlines mean you need an authorised spotter. Proximity to a house might demand a crane, costing $300 an hour plus travel. If the work affects a footpath or road, you’ll need a traffic management plan, which can cost over $1,000 for the day. Always check for council permits and underground services before you start. The Safe Work Australia 'Guide to managing risks of tree trimming and removal work' is your go-to for compliance.

faqs.question: How deep should I quote for stump grinding?
faqs.answer: It depends on what the client wants to do next. For laying new turf, grinding 150-200mm below ground level is usually enough. If they plan to replant a tree or build over the area, you need to go deeper, at least 300-400mm, to get the main root ball. Clarify this upfront, as grinding an extra 200mm can double the time and cost.

faqs.question: Does the type of tree change the quoting price?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. A soft pine is quick to cut but a dense hardwood like an Ironbark will wear out your chains and take more time and fuel. Palm trees produce a huge volume of fibrous, heavy waste that’s hard to chip and costs a lot to dump. Always identify the species, as a hardwood can easily add 25% to your labour time.

faqs.question: Who organises the council permit for tree removal?
faqs.answer: The homeowner is ultimately responsible for securing any required council permits. However, you should always ask to see the approved permit before starting work. Offering to handle the application process for the client can be a good value-add service. Just be sure to list it as a separate line item on your quote, as the paperwork takes time.

carpet-cleaning-quote-template.intro: This carpet cleaning quote template is for residential and small commercial jobs. It covers everything from a standard three-bedroom house to a small office space. Most cleaners get quotes wrong in two places: underestimating the time and chemicals needed for tough stains, and not charging extra for moving heavy furniture. A good quote protects your time and profit by setting clear expectations from the start.
