Use this template to make sure you've covered all your costs and look professional to the client, helping you win the job at the right price.

sections.heading: How to Price Your Steam Clean: Per Room vs. Square Metre
sections.body: Your main choice is pricing per room or per square metre. For standard homes, pricing per room is faster. A typical rate is $30-$40 per standard room (up to 12 sqm). For large open-plan areas or commercial jobs, use a square metre rate, usually around $3-$5 per sqm. Your labour is the biggest cost, so factor in travel, setup, and pack-down time. Chemical costs are small per job but add up. A 5L bottle of Prochem Carpet Prespray might cost $50 from a supplier like Cleanstar but will cover multiple jobs. Using an app like QuoteMate helps track these material costs accurately against each job.

sections.heading: Forgotten Costs That Kill Your Carpet Cleaning Margin
sections.body: A minimum call-out fee is essential for small jobs. Set one at around $90-$120 to make sure a single-room job is worth your time. Always add a line item for moving heavy furniture; anything bigger than a coffee table should attract a fee of $20-$50. Don't forget access issues. Quoting for a third-floor apartment with no lift requires more time and effort than a ground-floor house. Finally, specialised treatments for pet urine, ink, or red wine are not standard. Price them separately and explain that success isn't guaranteed. All your work should meet the AS/NZS 3733:2018 standard.

faqs.question: Do I need to charge extra for moving furniture?
faqs.answer: Yes. Your standard per-room price should only include moving light items like small tables or chairs. For heavy furniture like sofas, beds, or bookcases, you must charge extra. Add a separate line item on your quote for 'Heavy Furniture Moving', typically priced between $20 to $50 per large item. Be clear about this upfront.

faqs.question: How should I quote for really tough stains like pet urine?
faqs.answer: Quote specialised stain removal as a separate line item. Never include it in your standard clean price. For pet urine, red wine, or ink, charge an additional $30-$80 per area, depending on severity. Importantly, you should state that you're charging for the treatment process, not for guaranteed removal, as some stains can be permanent.

faqs.question: Is there an Australian Standard for professional carpet cleaning?
faqs.answer: Yes, AS/NZS 3733:2018 outlines the correct procedures for cleaning textile floor coverings. Referencing this standard in your quote shows you're a professional who follows industry best practice. It helps justify your price against cheaper competitors and gives the client confidence you'll care for their carpet properly. It's a key part of a professional quote.

bathroom-tiling-quote-template.intro: Quoting bathroom tiling isn't just about square metres. This bathroom tiling quote template is built for Australian tilers doing residential renos and new builds. Most quotes go wrong in two places: underestimating the demolition and prep work for old, uneven surfaces, and not charging a premium for complex tile patterns. Get those two things right and you'll protect your margin. This template has the line items to cover your costs for prep, waterproofing checks, laying, grouting, and finishing, so you don't leave money on the table or end up working for free.

sections.heading: Calculating Your Real Costs on a Bathroom Tiling Job
sections.body: Your labour rate per square metre is the core of your quote. For standard 600x300mm ceramic tiles on a clean, plumb wall, you might charge $60-$70/sqm. But for intricate mosaic sheets or a herringbone pattern, you should be charging upwards of $120/sqm to cover the extra cutting and layout time. Don't forget prep work – grinding a high spot on the slab or applying a primer is billable time. For materials, a 20kg bag of Davco flexible adhesive from a trade supplier costs about $40 and covers around 6sqm. Always add 15-20% for tile waste on complex patterns, not just the standard 10%.

sections.heading: What Most Tilers Forget to Add to a Bathroom Quote
sections.body: The biggest mistake is quoting the tiling but forgetting the work around it. Are you removing the old tiles? That's a separate line item for demolition and rubbish removal, which can cost $200-$300 for a small skip bin. Did you factor in protecting the client's floors from your work area to the front door? Add a charge for floor protection. Always check the waterproofing meets AS 3740 standards before you start; if it doesn't, quoting to fix it is a separate, crucial step. Also, add a line item for applying silicone to all internal corners and junctions after grouting is complete.

faqs.question: How much extra should I charge for herringbone or mosaic patterns?
faqs.answer: For complex patterns like herringbone or small mosaics, add 50-100% to your standard square metre labour rate. The extra time for cuts, layout, and grouting is significant. If your standard rate is $65/sqm, you should be quoting between $95-$130/sqm for these detailed jobs. Your quote should specify this as a separate rate.

faqs.question: Do I need to quote for screeding the floor?
faqs.answer: Yes, always quote screeding as a separate line item if the floor requires it. It's a separate task involving labour and materials that isn't part of tiling itself. Check the floor levels on your site visit. A standard bathroom floor might need 3-5 bags of sand and cement mix, which costs about $10 per bag from CSR.

faqs.question: Who is responsible for checking the waterproofing before I tile?
faqs.answer: You are. Before you lay a single tile, you must ensure the waterproofing is sound and compliant. If you tile over a faulty membrane, you can be held liable for fixing the resulting leaks. Always inspect the substrate, check for a compliance certificate from the waterproofer, and document its condition according to AS 3740.

concrete-slab-quote-template.intro: This concrete slab quote template is built for house slabs, shed bases, and driveways. Use it to get your line items right every time. Most concreters get the basics down but lose money on two things: underestimating waste and forgetting to charge for difficult site access. A cheap job can turn expensive fast if you need a concrete pump because the truck can't get close, or if you have to cart away an extra half-dozen barrows of soil by hand. This template helps you price for the job as it is, not as you hope it will be.

sections.heading: How to Price Your Slab: M3, Labour, and Waste
sections.body: Your main cost is the concrete itself, priced per cubic metre (m3). An N25 mix from a supplier like Boral or Hanson will run you about $300-$350 per m3 delivered. Always add a waste factor of 5-10% to your total volume to account for uneven ground and spillage. For labour, you can charge a day rate per person or a square metre rate for the whole job, from prep to finish. A typical rate for a simple slab finish is $50-$85 per square metre, including labour and materials. Always factor in reo mesh like SL72 from a trade supplier at around $100 per sheet.

sections.heading: What Gets Left Off a Concrete Slab Quote
sections.body: The biggest mistake is forgetting pump hire. If the truck can't reach the pour area, you'll need a line or boom pump, costing anywhere from $500 to over $1,000. Another forgotten cost is soil and rock disposal. Tip fees are high, so calculate the volume of spoil accurately and charge for it. Always check if a council permit is needed, as this adds time and cost. Finally, make sure your work meets the standard. All residential slabs must comply with AS 2870, which dictates things like slab thickness and reinforcement placement. Quoting to standard protects you and the client.

faqs.question: How much reo mesh overlap do I need?
faqs.answer: You need to overlap reinforcement mesh by at least two full squares to ensure structural integrity and prevent cracks. For SL72 mesh, with its 200mm grid, that means a 400mm overlap. Factor this into your total sheet count when ordering from a supplier like CSR, otherwise you'll come up short on the day.

faqs.question: When should I use N25 concrete over N20?
faqs.answer: Use N20 (20MPa) for footpaths and basic shed slabs. For anything structural like a house slab or a driveway that needs to support vehicles, you must use N25 (25MPa) or stronger. The price difference is minimal for the extra strength required. Most engineers will specify N25 as the minimum for residential slabs under AS 2870.

faqs.question: Do I need to quote for control joints?
faqs.answer: Yes, always. Control joints manage natural cracking as the concrete cures. For a basic broom-finish slab, saw cuts are the cheapest method. They should be cut within 24 hours of the pour to a depth of about one-quarter of the slab's thickness. Omitting them from the quote means you'll either wear the cost or have to ask the client for more money later.

kitchen-splashback-quote-template.intro: This kitchen splashback quote template is for Australian glaziers pricing up jobs for residential renos and new builds. It suits standard toughened glass installations in kitchens, laundries, and butler's pantries. Most quotes go wrong in two places: forgetting to charge per-item for GPO and switch cutouts, and not factoring in the extra labour for out-of-square walls. Getting these details right from the start protects your margin on the whole job. A clear, itemised quote prevents arguments with the builder or homeowner later, ensuring you get paid without hassle for the work you've actually done.

sections.heading: Pricing Toughened Glass, Cutouts, and Labour
sections.body: Your biggest cost is the glass itself. Price 6mm toughened Starphire or similar low-iron glass at around $350-$500 per square metre, supplied from your processor. Don't forget to add a per-item charge for cutouts; a standard double GPO cutout is about $60-$80. Labour for a straightforward splashback should be 3-4 hours for two glaziers, covering the site measure and the final installation. At $110/hour per person, that’s $660-$880 in labour. Add costs for consumables like high-grade neutral cure silicone, such as Bostik V60 from a trade supplier. Using a quoting app like QuoteMate helps you build these line items fast so nothing gets missed.

sections.heading: What Glaziers Forget on a Splashback Quote
sections.body: Leaving items off the quote is leaving money on the table. Always include a line item for polished edges, typically charged per lineal metre. Specify the paint finish; a 2-pack polyurethane colour backing costs more than standard vinyl and should be quoted accordingly. If you have to remove an old tile splashback, charge for the labour and tip fees. Difficult site access, like a 10th-floor apartment with no lift, requires its own line item for the extra time. Finally, make sure your installation complies with AS 1288-2006 for glass in buildings, especially regarding clearances for gas cooktops. This standard is not optional.

faqs.question: How much extra should I quote for metallic paint?
faqs.answer: Metallic and pearlescent finishes require more expensive pigments and extra prep work. You should add 20-30% to your normal colour-backing price. Quote it as a separate line item so the client sees the value. Always get a sample approved before ordering the glass, as metallic colours can look different under kitchen lighting.

faqs.question: Is there a standard for glass behind a gas cooktop?
faqs.answer: Yes. The glass must be Grade A toughened safety glass, usually 6mm, compliant with AS/NZS 2208. It also needs to meet the clearance requirements specified by the cooktop manufacturer, which is often detailed in their installation manual. Failure to meet these specs can cause the glass to crack from thermal stress and is a major compliance issue.

faqs.question: Do I charge for a check measure visit?
faqs.answer: You should factor the cost of one site visit for a check measure into your labour total. If a client, builder, or cabinet maker makes changes after you’ve measured, you are justified in charging a call-out fee for a second measure. This covers your time and travel, which can easily be $150-$200.

render-house-quote-template.intro: This house rendering quote template is for renderers pricing jobs on brick, block, or fibre cement sheet walls. Most quotes go wrong in two places: underestimating the prep work on old, painted surfaces, and not factoring in the full cost of scaffold hire for multi-storey homes. Get those right, and you protect your margin. This template helps you price every line item correctly, from masking the windows to the final texture coat, so you can send quotes that are fair for the client and profitable for your business.

sections.heading: How to Calculate Your Per-Metre Rate for Rendering
sections.body: Your square metre (sqm) rate is mostly labour. A good renderer can prep and apply a base coat to about 20-25 sqm per day. At a labour rate of $70/hr, that’s around $25/sqm in labour alone. Materials come next. A 20kg bag of cement render base from a trade supplier costs about $15 and covers 2.5 sqm, so that's $6/sqm. Add primer and a texture coat like Dulux AcraTex, plus a 10% waste factor. Your total cost might be $40-$60/sqm before overheads and profit. Using a quoting tool like QuoteMate helps track these material costs against live supplier pricing so your rate is always current.

sections.heading: What Gets Left Off a House Rendering Quote
sections.body: It’s the extras that eat your profit. Always include a line item for waste disposal; a 2-cubic-metre skip bin from a local supplier will cost you $300-$450. Scaffolding hire is another big one, often running $30-$50 per linear metre for the first week. Don't forget the non-billable labour of masking every window, door, and downpipe, which can take half a day. Finally, include substrate cleaning. A high-pressure wash is essential for proper adhesion, as specified by most render manufacturers. If you skip quoting these, you're doing them for free. Add them as separate line items so the client sees the value.

faqs.question: How much extra should I quote for a texture finish versus a smooth one?
faqs.answer: A texture coat requires more skill and often an extra pass, adding 20-30% to your labour time. The material is also pricier. A 15L pail of Dulux AcraTex 951 costs around $160 from a Dulux Trade Centre, whereas a standard cement render topcoat is much cheaper. Factor in at least a 25% price increase for acrylic texture finishes.

faqs.question: Do I need to charge for corner beads separately?
faqs.answer: Yes, always list external corner beads as a separate line item per linear metre. They protect edges from chipping and are essential for a sharp, professional finish. PVC beads from a trade supplier cost $6-$9 per 3-metre length, but the main cost is the labour to set them perfectly straight before rendering.

faqs.question: What's a fair contingency to add for patching old brickwork?
faqs.answer: For older homes with crumbling mortar or visible cracks, a 15% contingency on your prep labour is a safe bet. You can't see the full extent of damage until after the pressure wash. Specify in your quote that this covers minor patching, and that extensive structural repairs will be quoted as a variation to the contract.

plasterboard-installation-quote-template.intro: This plasterboard installation quote template is for Aussie plasterers pricing new builds, renovations, or patch jobs. Most quotes go wrong in two places: underestimating the labour for setting and sanding three full coats, or completely forgetting rubbish disposal costs for the old walls. Using a proper template makes sure you price every line item, from the Gyprock sheets and cornice cement down to the tip fees. It helps you protect your margin and deliver a professional quote that wins the work without costing you money. Get the numbers right from the start.

sections.heading: How to Calculate Your Square Metre Rate for Plastering
sections.body: Your price depends on the finish level, but a good starting point for a standard Level 4 finish is $45 to $65 per square metre (m2), supply and install. This covers materials like 10mm Gyprock Plus sheets from CSR, screws, paper tape, and compounds. It also includes your labour for hanging, setting three coats, and sanding. For a small reno, you might charge by the day instead, say $600-$800 plus materials. Always measure walls and ceilings separately and add a 10-15% waste factor on your sheet count. For premium materials like soundproof or fire-rated board, price them as separate line items as they can double your material cost per sheet.

sections.heading: What Plasterers Forget to Add to Their Quotes
sections.body: The biggest mistake is forgetting site prep and cleanup. If you're ripping out old lath and plaster, you need to quote for a skip bin and the labour to fill it. Another common miss is access equipment. If you're working on a raked ceiling or in a stairwell, the cost of hiring a scissor lift or mobile scaffold must be on the quote. Also, specify the level of finish you're providing. Most domestic work is Level 4, but if the job has lots of critical light, the client might expect a Level 5 finish, which takes more time and material. Always specify this to avoid arguments, as defined in AS/NZS 2589:2017.

faqs.question: How much waste should I factor in for plasterboard sheets?
faqs.answer: For a standard square room, a 10% waste factor is usually safe. If the room has lots of angles, windows, or doors, increase that to 15%. It’s better to have one sheet left over than to make a second trip to your supplier for a single offcut. Always calculate your waste factor at 15% for complex jobs.

faqs.question: Does moisture-resistant board cost much more to install?
faqs.answer: The installation labour is the same, but the material cost is higher. A sheet of Gyprock Aquachek from CSR for wet areas can be 30-50% more expensive than a standard Gyprock Plus sheet of the same size. Always price the specific board per sheet and list it as a separate material cost on your quote to show the client the price difference.

faqs.question: How should I price cornice installation?
faqs.answer: Price cornice per linear metre (LM), including supply, adhesive, and installation labour. For a standard 90mm cove cornice, a fair rate is between $10 and $15 per LM. More decorative or oversized profiles will cost more in both materials and labour, so get a current supply price from a supplier like CSR before finalising your quote.

paving-quote-template.intro: This paving quote template is for landscapers pricing residential jobs like paths, patios, and driveways. It suits projects using clay, concrete, or natural stone pavers. Most quotes go wrong in two places: underestimating the labour for site prep and excavation, and completely forgetting the cost of soil disposal. A tight, accurate quote shows the client you know your stuff and protects your margin from getting eaten up by unexpected tip fees. Use this paving quote template to make sure every cost is covered before you send the price to the customer and start the job.

sections.heading: How to Price Paving Labour and Base Materials
sections.body: Your biggest cost is labour. Price it per square metre, not just per hour. A straightforward job might take two landscapers a day to prep and lay 20 square metres. At $80/hour per person, that's $1280 in labour, or $64 per square metre. Next, price your base materials. A tonne of road base from a local landscape supplier will set you back about $80-$100, and bedding sand is around $90-$110 per tonne. Don't guess these prices. Using an app like QuoteMate to pull current supplier costs ensures your material quote is accurate to the dollar. Always add a 5-10% waste factor on pavers and sand.

sections.heading: What to Add for Site Access and Waste Disposal
sections.body: Don't get caught out by site costs. If access is tight, you'll need to price in a mini-excavator and dumper hire, which can be $400-$500 a day. If you're digging out an old path or lawn, you have to pay to get rid of it. A 3-cubic-metre skip bin for clean fill costs around $350, but if it's mixed with concrete or other rubbish, the price can double. Check local council rules too; some require permits or specific stormwater management which adds cost. These are separate line items, not overheads. List them clearly so the client sees what they're paying for. Tip fees are often charged by weight.

faqs.question: How much extra should I quote for a herringbone pattern?
faqs.answer: A herringbone pattern requires more cuts, which means more labour and more waste. Increase your labour estimate by 15-20% to cover the extra time at the wet saw. You should also increase your paver waste calculation from the standard 5% up to around 10% to account for all the angled offcuts.

faqs.question: Do I need to include paver sealing in the main quote?
faqs.answer: No, paver sealing should be an optional extra. Present it as a separate line item with a clear price. It shows you're thorough and gives the client a choice. A good penetrating sealer from Crommelin or a similar brand from a trade supplier will cost around $120 for a 4-litre tin, plus your labour to apply it.

faqs.question: What's a fair price for just the excavation and base preparation?
faqs.answer: For a standard site with good machine access, budget around $50 to $70 per square metre. This covers digging out the area, supplying and laying the road base and sand, and compacting it properly. If you hit rock or have to move material by wheelbarrow, that price can easily climb past $100 per square metre.

ev-charger-installation-quote-template.intro: Quoting an EV charger install isn't just about the unit. The biggest costs come from long cable runs and old switchboards needing an upgrade. This EV charger installation quote template is for electricians pricing residential or small commercial jobs. It helps you account for the real variables, like the difference between a simple garage install next to the board and a 20-metre run through wall cavities. Get the cable length and switchboard assessment right, and you'll protect your margin on every install. This guide adds the pricing details you'll need to quote accurately.

sections.heading: How to Price the Cable Run and Switchboard Work
sections.body: The charger unit cost is fixed, but the cable and switchboard are where you make or lose money. A typical 15-metre run of 6mm² TPS cable from an electrical wholesaler like TLE will cost you around $90 in materials. Labour for a straightforward install in a garage might be two hours. A job needing a 30-metre run through a double-brick cavity could easily take five hours. At $110/hr, that's a $330 difference in labour alone. Always check the switchboard first. A new Type A RCBO is about $60, but if the board is full or has old ceramic fuses, you must quote for an upgrade, which can add $800 or more.

sections.heading: What Sparkies Forget on an EV Charger Quote
sections.body: Forgetting to charge for testing and commissioning is a classic mistake. Setting up the charger on the client's Wi-Fi, walking them through the app, and performing mandatory tests takes at least 30 minutes. Also, factor in the cost of issuing a Certificate of Compliance for Electrical Work. Another trap is underestimating difficult access. Quoting a simple run and then finding you need to spend an hour fishing cable through an insulated wall will kill your profit. Clearly state what's not included, like plaster repair or painting. All electrical work must comply with AS/NZS 3000, including mandatory testing procedures you bill for.

faqs.question: How much more should I quote for a 22kW three-phase charger over a 7kW single-phase?
faqs.answer: A 22kW unit needs a three-phase supply. The charger itself is $300-$500 more than a 7kW model. The main cost increase is in the heavier cable and a three-pole breaker, adding at least $400-$600 in materials and extra labour. This assumes the site already has three-phase power available at the switchboard.

faqs.question: When does a switchboard need a mandatory upgrade for an EV charger?
faqs.answer: If the existing board is full, uses old ceramic fuses, or lacks a main isolating switch, it needs an upgrade. Any new circuit requires its own RCD or RCBO protection. If you can't add one safely to the existing board, you must quote to upgrade it to meet the current wiring rules in AS/NZS 3000.

faqs.question: Should I let the customer supply their own charger?
faqs.answer: It's risky. You lose the margin on supply and can't guarantee the quality or compliance of a unit bought online. It's better to supply a trusted brand like Zappi or Tesla from your wholesaler. If the customer insists, state clearly on your quote that your warranty covers workmanship only, not the customer-supplied hardware.

vinyl-plank-flooring-quote-template.intro: This vinyl plank flooring quote template is built for Australian tradies tackling residential and light commercial jobs. It's designed for quoting both floating click-systems and glue-down LVT installations. The two spots where quotes go wrong are subfloor preparation and trims. Underestimate the cost of levelling a concrete slab and you'll work for free. Forget to price 30 metres of scotia and transition bars, and you've just lost your profit on the job. This template ensures you account for every line item, from the planks to the disposal of old carpet, making your quote accurate.

sections.heading: Pricing Vinyl Planks: Labour and Material Costs
sections.body: Your main cost is the planks themselves. Expect to pay between $30/m² for basic hybrid planks off the shelf up to $70/m² for premium, thicker options from a flooring wholesaler. Always add a 10-15% waste factor for cuts; for a 50m² job, you need to buy and bill for at least 55m² of stock. Labour is your next key item. A straightforward installation on a clean, level subfloor should be quoted at around $35-$45 per square metre. If you have to do the floor prep, like grinding concrete or pulling up old flooring, that is a separate charge on top. A good starting point is to double your total material cost to get a rough price.

sections.heading: What Tradies Forget on a Vinyl Plank Quote
sections.body: Subfloor preparation is the number one missed cost. Grinding concrete high spots or pouring self-levelling compound adds significant time and material costs. A single bag of leveller from CSR might cost $50 and only cover a small area. Second, always add a line item for furniture removal and replacement. Don't do it for free. Third is the disposal of old flooring. Tip fees for carpet and underlay are a direct cost you must pass on to the customer. Finally, difficult cuts around door jambs or stair nosings take more time than open floor, so factor that in. Your work should meet the requirements of AS 1884-2012 for resilient floor coverings.

faqs.question: How much waste should I factor in for vinyl planks?
faqs.answer: A flat 10% is the standard for rooms with simple layouts. For jobs with multiple angles, hallways, or for a herringbone pattern, increase that to 15%. On a 60m² job, that's an extra 6m² to 9m² of planks you must include in the material cost on your quote.

faqs.question: Do I charge extra for subfloor levelling?
faqs.answer: Yes, always. Subfloor prep is a separate line item and is never included in the per-metre installation rate. A bag of levelling compound like Ardex K 15 covers about 5m² at a 3mm thickness and costs around $45 from trade suppliers, plus your labour to mix and apply it.

faqs.question: Is quoting for glue-down LVT different from a floating floor?
faqs.answer: Yes. Glue-down planks require more labour for trowelling the adhesive and a longer installation time. You must also add the cost of the glue itself, which can be over $120 for a 15-litre tub. A floating click-lock system is faster, so your labour charge per square metre will be lower.

commercial-cleaning-quote-template.intro: This commercial cleaning quote template is for regular contract work in small to medium Australian offices. It's not for one-off bond cleans or specialised medical facilities. Most cleaners lose money in two spots: under-pricing consumables like soap and paper towels, and not allowing enough time for high-traffic areas like kitchens and bathrooms. Get those two right and your weekly run will actually turn a profit. A tight, professional quote shows the client you know your stuff and helps you win the job without sacrificing your margin from the start.

sections.heading: How to Price Per Square Metre vs By the Hour
sections.body: Price either per square metre or by the hour. A basic office clean runs $2-$4 per square metre, monthly. For hourly, charge $45-$65 per cleaner, per hour, plus GST. The rate depends on the tasks. A simple vacuum and bin empty is cheaper than a full kitchen and bathroom sanitisation. Don’t forget your materials. A 5L bottle of commercial-grade floor cleaner from a supplier like Blackwoods costs about $30 and will cover a certain area. Track these costs. An app like QuoteMate can store your material costs and add them to each job, ensuring you always cover your overheads.

sections.heading: What Gets Left Off a Commercial Cleaning Quote
sections.body: The first 'deep clean' is often forgotten. The initial clean always takes longer than a standard maintenance clean. Quote it as a separate, one-off charge. Also, specify what's not included in the regular price, like periodic steam cleaning of carpets or high-reach window cleaning. These should be quoted as separate services performed quarterly or annually. Another miss is access. If you need special keys, security passes, or after-hours alarm codes, any time spent organising this is billable. Finally, check if the building management charges for waste disposal or skip bin usage.

faqs.question: Should I charge extra for weekend or after-hours cleaning?
faqs.answer: Yes. Your labour costs are higher outside of standard business hours. A weekend or after-hours job should have a loading of at least 25-50% on your standard hourly rate. Public holidays are usually double-time. Make this a clear line item on your quote so the client understands the price difference. Always check the Cleaning Services Award [MA000022] for current rates.

faqs.question: Do I need my own public liability insurance?
faqs.answer: Yes, it is essential. Most commercial building managers will not allow you on site without a Certificate of Currency showing at least $10 million in public liability coverage. This cost is a business overhead that should be factored into your charge-out rate, not added as a separate fee. You cannot operate professionally without it.

faqs.question: Who pays for cleaning equipment like vacuums?
faqs.answer: You do. The cleaning contractor is expected to provide all necessary equipment, from vacuums and mops to cloths and chemicals. You are also responsible for ensuring it's safe and compliant, including regular electrical testing and tagging for any powered gear. These equipment costs are part of your overheads, covered by your hourly or square metre rate.

smoke-alarm-installation-quote-template.intro: This smoke alarm installation quote template is for Australian electricians quoting residential jobs, from single-unit replacements to full home upgrades meeting new state laws. It's built for quoting interconnected photoelectric alarms, both hardwired and wireless. The two places sparkies get quotes wrong are underestimating labour for difficult access in older homes and forgetting to charge for testing and the compliance certificate. Using this template helps you price every component accurately, ensuring your quote covers the full scope of work required under Australian Standards and protects your margin on the job.

sections.heading: How to Price Labour and Materials for Smoke Alarm Installs
sections.body: The alarm unit itself is just the start. A good quality interconnected alarm like the Clipsal Fire Tek 755RLPSMA4 costs about $75 from an electrical wholesaler. The real variable is labour. A simple swap of an existing hardwired alarm might take 30 minutes. But installing a new hardwired point in a double-brick house with poor roof access could take two hours. Price your labour per point, not per house. Factor in $5-$10 per alarm for consumables like cable, screws, and wall plugs. For a standard three-bedroom home, quoting 3-4 hours of labour plus materials is a safe starting point for a fully hardwired system from scratch.

sections.heading: What Sparkies Forget on a Smoke Alarm Quote
sections.body: Forgetting small items kills your profit. Always include a line item for removing and disposing of old alarms, especially ionisation models. Add 15-30 minutes of labour for testing the interconnected system once installed – walking around with a broom handle to test each unit. High ceilings or tricky access points might require special ladders or a mobile scaffold; this is a hire cost that belongs on the quote. Most importantly, charge for your compliance certificate. It's a legal document tied to your licence. Your final installation must meet all requirements of AS 3786:2014, so that certificate has real value.

faqs.question: Should I quote for hardwired or wireless interconnected alarms?
faqs.answer: Quote both if you can. Wireless units cost more upfront; a Clipsal 755RFB2 wireless base is around $120 versus $20 for a standard one. However, they save significant labour time, especially in multi-storey or difficult-to-access homes. Presenting both options lets the customer decide between material cost and labour cost. Either way, the installation must comply with AS 3786:2014.

faqs.question: How much do I charge for the compliance certificate?
faqs.answer: Never give it away for free. It's a critical part of the service that carries legal weight. Most electricians add a separate line item for the Certificate of Compliance, typically between $50 and $95 plus GST. This fee covers your time to complete the paperwork correctly and, where required, lodge it with the state's electrical safety authority. It's a professional service, not just a piece of paper.

faqs.question: What happens if I discover asbestos during the install?
faqs.answer: Stop work immediately. Your quote should have a clause excluding hazardous material handling. Inform the client that the site is unsafe to continue and that a licensed asbestos removalist is now required. You cannot drill, cut, or disturb suspected asbestos-containing materials. All work must halt until the area is certified safe by a professional, as required by Safe Work Australia guidelines.

wardrobe-fitout-quote-template.intro: This built-in wardrobe quote template is for cabinet-makers pricing custom jobs, from simple reach-ins to full walk-in fit-outs. Most quotes go wrong in two areas: underestimating the cost of quality hardware like soft-close runners, and forgetting to price demolition and disposal of the old unit. Get these right and your margin is protected. This guide covers the key cost drivers and common mistakes to help you build a solid quote that wins work without costing you money.

sections.heading: How to Price Carcass, Doors, and Labour
sections.body: Price your carcass material by the sheet. A 2400x1200mm sheet of 16mm white melamine from Laminex or Polytec will set you back about $50-$70 plus GST. Factor in a 15-20% waste allowance, more for complex cuts. Hardware is a major variable. A pair of standard drawer runners is cheap, but quality soft-close runners from Hafele can be $50 per drawer. Labour for a standard 2.4m two-door wardrobe is typically 8-12 hours for manufacture in the workshop and 4-6 hours for site installation. At $90/hour, that's over a grand in labour alone.

sections.heading: What Gets Left Off a Wardrobe Quote
sections.body: Forgetting demolition and disposal is the biggest mistake. Removing an old wardrobe and a trip to the tip can easily cost $250. Quote it as a separate line item. Site prep is another. Does the wall behind the old unit need patching and painting? Clarify who is responsible. If the client wants internal lighting, you’ll need a licensed electrician. This is not your job; you just need to allow for their access and cost. While there's no specific installation standard, building to the principles in AS/NZS 4785 for cabinet components shows good workmanship.

faqs.question: How much should I budget for material waste?
faqs.answer: A safe range is 15-20% for material waste on a standard job. For designs with many small components or angled cuts, you might push this to 25%. Always quote based on buying full sheets from your supplier, as you can't buy half a sheet of 16mm melamine from Polytec or Laminex.

faqs.question: Should my quote include patching and painting?
faqs.answer: Generally, no. A cabinet-maker’s job is the wardrobe. Your quote should clearly state that making good any wall surfaces after removing the old unit is the client's responsibility or will be quoted separately. This avoids arguments later. The only exception is if you explicitly offer it as part of a complete renovation service.

faqs.question: What’s the real cost difference between hinged and sliding doors?
faqs.answer: Sliding doors are almost always more expensive due to the track system. A basic set of tracks and rollers for a 2.4m opening from a supplier like Lincoln Sentry can add $200-$400 to the material cost compared to using three or four standard cabinet hinges on a pair of hinged doors.

stump-grinding-quote-template.intro: This stump grinding quote template is for Australian arborists pricing residential and small commercial jobs. It covers everything from single backyard stumps to clearing a few for a new driveway. Most quotes go wrong on two things: underestimating the time needed for dense hardwood stumps like ironbark, and forgetting to price the green waste disposal correctly. Getting these two items right is the difference between making a profit or doing the job for wages. Use this template to build an accurate quote that covers your costs and protects your margin every time you fire up the grinder.

sections.heading: How to Calculate Your Stump Grinding Rate
sections.body: The standard way to price is per centimetre of diameter, measured at the widest point at ground level. A common rate is $3.50 to $5.00 per cm, plus GST. This method scales well, but always have a minimum call-out fee, like $180, to cover travel and setup for small jobs. For big or tricky stumps, an hourly rate of $150-$220 might work better. Remember to factor in grinder tooth wear, which costs about $10-$15 per hour of use, plus fuel. Using software like QuoteMate helps you add these as standard line items so you never forget them.

sections.heading: What Gets Left Off a Stump Grinding Quote
sections.body: Forgetting to check for underground services is the most expensive mistake. Always do a free Dial Before You Dig search before starting. Limited site access is another classic. If you can't get your Vermeer grinder through a narrow gate, you'll need to price for a smaller machine or manual work. Also, specify the backfill material. Leaving the grindings in the hole is cheapest, but trucking in clean soil from a supplier like Australian Native Landscapes costs money. Finally, state your grinding depth. Anything deeper than a standard 150mm will take longer and should be quoted as an extra.

faqs.question: Do I have to call Dial Before You Dig for a small stump?
faqs.answer: Yes, every time. Hitting a water pipe or Telstra cable will cost you thousands and ruin your reputation. The client won't care how small the stump was. The Dial Before You Dig service is free, takes minutes online, and provides a report showing the location of registered utilities. It's your professional responsibility to check before you grind.

faqs.question: How deep do you need to grind for replanting?
faqs.answer: For laying new turf, grinding 150mm below the final ground level is usually enough to stop regrowth. If the client wants to plant a new tree in the same spot, you need to go much deeper, around 400-600mm, to remove the entire root ball. This takes significantly more time, so price it as a separate, higher-cost line item.

faqs.question: How should I price the green waste removal?
faqs.answer: Stump grindings expand in volume, so a small stump can create a full ute load of mulch. Check your local council tip fees for green waste, which can be $70-$120 per load. Price this as a separate line item on your quote. Alternatively, offer the client a discount to keep the grindings on-site for use as garden mulch.

bathroom-waterproofing-quote-template.intro: This bathroom waterproofing quote template is for builders and waterproofers on domestic wet area jobs. It suits standard renovations and new builds. Most tradies get tripped up quoting two things: the labour for proper substrate preparation, which can vary wildly, and forgetting to price in the compliance certificate and the liability that comes with it. Get those two items right and you’ll protect your margin. This template helps you remember every line item so you can quote accurately and get on with the job.

sections.heading: How to Price Waterproofing Labour and Materials
sections.body: For a standard bathroom, think per square metre. A typical job is around 10-15m² including the floor, shower walls, and hob. Your main cost is the membrane. A 15L pail of Crommelin Shower Waterproofing Membrane from a trade supplier costs about $215 and covers roughly 10m² for two coats. Factor in primer, bond breaker tape, and reinforcing fabric, adding another $80-$100. Labour is the biggest variable. Allow 4-6 hours at your standard rate, say $70/hr, for prep and two coats. All up, you should be quoting around $750-$1000 for a standard bathroom, depending on site conditions.

sections.heading: What Tradies Forget on a Waterproofing Quote
sections.body: The biggest mistake is quoting for a perfect surface. Most bathroom floors need grinding or a skim coat before you can even open the primer. Add a line item for substrate preparation. Second, tradies forget the cost of compliance. You're signing a legal document that says your work meets AS 3740-2010. This carries risk and insurance cost, so add $50-$150 for issuing the certificate. Using a quoting app like QuoteMate makes it easy to save these easily-forgotten items as standard line items. Finally, factor in travel time for the second coat, as you can’t do it all in one visit.

faqs.question: How do I quote for different substrates like concrete vs FC sheet?
faqs.answer: A porous concrete slab needs more primer than fibre cement sheet. Budget for an extra litre of primer and 30 minutes of labour if you’re working on old, thirsty concrete. Always inspect the site first. Villaboard is straightforward, but old concrete can hide problems. Check the specific membrane's data sheet, like for Davco K10, for primer requirements.

faqs.question: Should I charge extra for flood testing?
faqs.answer: Yes, always. Flood testing takes time. You have to dam the doorway, fill the area with water for 24 hours, then drain and dry it. This adds at least half a day of site visits and follow-up. Price it as a separate line item for $200-$300, as it's a critical quality check under AS 3740.

faqs.question: How much waste should I factor in for membrane and tape?
faqs.answer: Add a 10% waste factor for your liquid membrane, as some always gets left in the pail or dries on rollers. For reinforcing tape and bond breakers, add 15%, especially for complex layouts with multiple corners or niches. It's better to have a bit left over than to stop the job for another trip to the supplier.

garage-door-replacement-quote-template.intro: This garage door replacement quote template is for tradies installing standard residential roller and sectional doors. It covers the essential line items for a clean, profitable job. Most installers get stung in two places: underestimating labour on sites with poor access, and forgetting to charge for the removal and disposal of the old steel door and motor. This guide helps you price those items correctly so your quote is accurate and you don't work for free. A tight quote on labour and waste protects your margin on the whole job.

sections.heading: How to Price Labour and Disposal for a Standard Roller Door
sections.body: A single-car roller door replacement is a two-person job. Budget for two installers for 3 to 4 hours on site. At a rate of $90 per hour per person, that's $540 to $720 in labour. The door itself, a standard single Colorbond roller from a supplier like B&D Doors, will cost you around $900. A quality motor, like a Merlin SilentDrive Essential, adds another $500. Don't forget disposal. The old steel door is heavy and awkward. Your local council tip will charge a fee, so add a line item for at least $80-$120 to cover the tip fee, your time, and fuel.

sections.heading: What Gets Left Off: Structural Fixes and Electrical Work
sections.body: Old garages often have problems. The timber jambs the new tracks mount to might be rotten or warped. You must inspect this first. If it needs fixing, add a line item for 'remedial frame repairs' – this can be a few hundred dollars in timber and labour. The new motor needs a GPO within a metre. If there isn't one, you'll need a licensed sparkie to install it. This is a separate cost, usually $250-$350, that must be on the quote to avoid arguments later. All wiring must comply with AS/NZS 3000. Also, note if the garage is full of the client's junk, as clearing a workspace costs you time.

faqs.question: How much contingency should I add for a custom-sized door?
faqs.answer: For custom-sized doors, add at least 20% to the door panel cost. Suppliers like Steel-Line or Gliderol charge a premium and have longer lead times. These orders are non-refundable if you mis-measure, so measure three times. Confirm the exact additional cost and lead time with your supplier before finalising your quote.

faqs.question: Do I need to quote for replacing the safety beams?
faqs.answer: Yes, always include new safety beams. Modern openers require them to meet Australian safety standards. Old beams are rarely compatible with new motors. A new pair of photoelectric (PE) beams is usually included in a motor kit from suppliers like ATA or Merlin, but always check the box contents before pricing.

faqs.question: Is removing an old tilt door more work than a roller door?
faqs.answer: Yes, much more. A tilt door's spring and counterweight assembly is heavy, bulky, and can be dangerous to dismantle. They are also harder to transport for disposal. You should add at least one to two extra hours of labour to your quote, around $180-$240, for removing an old tilt door.

ducted-aircon-quote-template.intro: Quoting ducted air conditioning is more than just the unit price. The real profit gets lost in tricky roof spaces and forgetting to charge for every single zone motor. This ducted air conditioning quote template is built for Aussie HVAC techs doing residential installs, from single-storey brick veneers to complex multi-level homes. It helps you remember the details that protect your margin, like difficult access charges and the labour for balancing every zone properly. Get the core costs right, and the job runs smoothly from start to finish.

sections.heading: How to Price the Unit, Ducting, and Labour
sections.body: A 14kW Daikin unit might cost you $4,500 from a supplier like Actrol, but that's just the start. The real cost is in the layout. Budget around $350-$500 per outlet for flexible ducting, plenum boxes, and diffusers. Labour is your biggest variable. A simple single-storey job might take two techs a full day, so that's 16 hours at your rate. For a tight roof space or a two-storey house, you might need to double that. Always add a 10% waste factor on flexible ducting; offcuts for tight bends are unavoidable. Your total install cost, before margin, for a 5-outlet system will often land between $8,000 and $11,000.

sections.heading: What Gets Left Off a Ducted AC Quote
sections.body: The biggest mistake is assuming the sparkie's work is minor. A dedicated circuit from the switchboard can cost $500-$900, especially in an older home. Always quote this separately. Don't forget crane hire for lifting the outdoor unit on multi-storey jobs, which can add another $400. Rubbish disposal for the old unit and packaging isn't free. Forgetting to add these items as line items in QuoteMate can wipe out your profit. Finally, include the cost of your Certificate of Compliance. All electrical work must comply with AS/NZS 3000, and all air con installs must meet the Building Code of Australia (BCA) ventilation requirements.

faqs.question: How much margin should I add to a ducted air con job?
faqs.answer: Start with a 15-20% margin on materials like the main unit and ductwork. For labour, your hourly rate should already have profit built in. On a full system install, aiming for a total job margin of 20-25% after all costs are covered is a solid target for most residential work.

faqs.question: Do I need to quote for different zones separately?
faqs.answer: Yes, always. Each zone needs a motorised damper, a wall controller or sensor, and extra labour for wiring and commissioning. A standard 240V damper from a supplier like Polyaire can cost over $100 plus your labour. Pricing per zone makes your quote transparent and prevents you from losing money.

faqs.question: What's the best way to handle warranty on the quote?
faqs.answer: Specify the manufacturer's warranty on parts (usually 5 years) and your own warranty on installation labour (typically 12 months) as separate items. This clarifies that a faulty fan motor is the manufacturer's responsibility to supply, protecting you from unpaid call-outs for parts failure after your labour warranty expires.

laundry-renovation-quote-template.intro: This laundry renovation quote template is for builders and cabinet makers pricing small-to-medium domestic jobs. It covers the basics, from cabinetry to tapware. Most tradies get tripped up on two things: underestimating the cost of moving plumbing even 300mm, and forgetting to price waterproofing to standard. A simple laundry can quickly become unprofitable if you don't account for the plumber's time to chase pipes or the membrane required for a new floor waste. This template helps you price those items correctly from the start.

sections.heading: How to Price the Real Cost Drivers in a Laundry Reno
sections.body: Your final price isn't just the flat-pack kitchen. Labour is the biggest variable. A plumber's call-out and first hour is around $250, plus $120 per hour after that. Moving a washing machine waste pipe is often a half-day of cutting, chasing, and making good. Always add a 15% waste factor on tiles, more for complex patterns. A simple laminate benchtop might be $300, but a 20mm engineered stone top for the same space will start at $800 from a stonemason. Keeping track of these supplier costs in real-time with an app like QuoteMate prevents margin loss on the job.

sections.heading: Forgetting These Items Will Cost You Money
sections.body: Demolition and waste disposal are the most common omissions. A small skip bin hire costs at least $300, and you need to factor in your labour to fill it. If the house is pre-1990, you must allow for asbestos testing on wall linings. Waterproofing is another big one. If you're adding a floor waste, the whole floor and wall junctions must comply with AS 3740. That means priming, applying two coats of membrane like Davco K10 Plus, and installing bond breakers in all corners. Also, remember to price for painting and patching the walls where old cupboards were removed. It all adds up.

faqs.question: How much extra should I quote to move a washing machine drain?
faqs.answer: Moving a drain 500mm can cost more than the new trough. Budget for at least 3-4 hours of a plumber's time plus materials. This usually involves cutting the wall or slab to re-route pipework. Expect to add between $500 and $900 to the plumbing bill for this change, before any wall repairs are done.

faqs.question: Does a laundry floor legally need to be waterproofed?
faqs.answer: Yes, if it has a floor waste. Australian Standard AS 3740 requires waterproofing for the full floor and relevant wall junctions in that case. For a laundry without a floor waste on a ground-floor slab, it's not mandatory but is good practice. For any laundry in an apartment or on a second storey, waterproofing is always required.

faqs.question: What’s the price difference for a small laminate vs. stone benchtop?
faqs.answer: For a typical 1.5 metre laundry bench, a pre-made laminate top from a trade supplier will cost around $200-$250 off the shelf. A basic 20mm engineered stone top for the same space, supplied and installed by a stonemason, will start around $750. It’s a significant jump in material cost you need to quote accurately.

outdoor-kitchen-quote-template.intro: This outdoor kitchen quote template is for builders pricing custom alfresco jobs, from a simple BBQ island to a full setup with a sink and fridge. Most quotes go wrong in two places: underestimating the cost of stone benchtop fabrication and forgetting the compliance certificates for gas and plumbing. A good template stops you from leaving money on the table. Use this to build accurate, professional quotes that cover every line item, from the first GPO to the last stainless steel hinge, so you can price the job right.

sections.heading: How to Price Stone Benchtops and Marine-Grade Cabinetry
sections.body: Benchtops are your biggest variable. A 20mm engineered stone top from a supplier like Caesarstone will run $800-$1200 per square metre, supplied and installed. Granite can be double that. Always get a firm quote from your stonemason that includes cutouts for the BBQ and sink. For cabinetry, marine-grade plywood is the standard for custom carcasses, costing around $150 per 2400x1200 sheet from a trade supplier. Factor in at least 20% for waste. Labour for a chippy to build and install custom cabinetry is typically billed at $80-$100 per hour. Don't forget stainless steel hardware; cheap hinges will rust within a year.

sections.heading: What Gets Left Off an Outdoor Kitchen Quote
sections.body: It’s the small things that kill your margin. First, gas fitting requires a licensed plumber and a compliance certificate under AS/NZS 5601. That’s a separate line item, often $400-$600. Second, waterproofing the wall behind the BBQ is critical, especially on timber-framed houses. Quote for Villaboard and a membrane that meets AS 3740. Third, waste disposal for stone offcuts isn’t cheap; your mason may charge extra for it. Finally, think about site access. If you can’t get a small crane or enough blokes to lift a 200kg stone benchtop into a backyard, your labour costs will blow out fast.

faqs.question: Do I need a council permit for an outdoor kitchen?
faqs.answer: Usually no, if it's not a fully enclosed structure. However, if you're building a new roofed pergola for it or running major new service lines, you might. The client should be responsible for checking with their local council before work commences, as rules vary significantly between areas.

faqs.question: How much should I allow for plumbing and electrical?
faqs.answer: For a setup with a sink, a few GPOs, and lighting, budget at least $1500-$2500. This covers labour and materials for a plumber to run water and waste, plus a sparky for a new circuit and outdoor-rated fittings. This cost is separate from the gas fitting compliance certificate, which is its own line item.

faqs.question: What's the best material for outdoor kitchen cabinets?
faqs.answer: Marine-grade plywood is the standard for durable, custom carcasses. For doors, you can use exterior-grade products like Laminex Alfresco Compact Laminate or specially treated timber. Avoid standard MDF or particleboard entirely. They will swell and fail within a year, even if they look protected from the rain. It's not worth the callback.

timber-floor-sanding-quote-template.intro: This is for flooring installers quoting timber floor sanding and polishing jobs in residential or light commercial sites. It works for common Aussie hardwoods like Spotted Gum and Blackbutt, as well as softer timbers like Pine. Most quotes go wrong by underestimating floor repairs and the number of polyurethane coats needed for a durable finish. A good timber floor sanding quote template separates the sanding price per square metre from the prep work, so you don't lose your margin fixing someone else's dodgy floorboards. Get the prep and finish right, and the price looks after itself.

sections.heading: How to Price Sanding and Coating by the Square Metre
sections.body: The standard charge for sanding and polishing is per square metre. For a straightforward job, this ranges from $30 to $50 per square metre (sqm) including GST. This price should cover three passes with the sander (coarse, medium, fine), punching nails, filling gaps with colour-matched putty, and applying three coats of polyurethane. Labour is your biggest cost, so base your rate on getting 30-40 sqm done per day. A 4-litre can of Cabot's CFP Floor Water Based from a trade supplier costs about $150 and covers roughly 40 sqm for one coat, so budget around $11-$12 per sqm for three coats of a quality finish.

sections.heading: What Gets Left Off a Floor Sanding Quote
sections.body: Forgetting the extras is where you lose money. Always list furniture removal as a separate line item, charging an hourly rate. If you have to pull up and dispose of old carpet and underlay, that's another cost—at least $5-$8 per sqm. Check for access issues; quoting a third-floor apartment with no lift is different from a ground-floor house. Also, specify the finish. A high-gloss finish shows every imperfection, requiring more prep time than a satin or matte finish. Your quote should state the number of coats included, typically three. Any extra coats requested by the client should be priced at around $8-$10 per sqm.

faqs.question: How much extra should I charge for staining a floor?
faqs.answer: Staining adds a full step to the process and requires more skill than a clear coat. You should add 20-30% to your standard square metre rate. A product like Feast Watson Prooftint from a trade supplier costs about $35 per 250ml, which covers roughly 10 sqm. Factor in the extra labour time for application and drying before the top coats go on.

faqs.question: Should I quote more for water-based or oil-based polyurethane?
faqs.answer: Yes, water-based polyurethane is usually more expensive per can but dries much faster, allowing multiple coats in a day. Oil-based is cheaper but has a longer cure time. Price water-based finishes about 10-15% higher per square metre to cover the higher material cost. For example, Cabot's water-based is around $150 for 4L, while the oil-based equivalent is closer to $120.

faqs.question: How do I price major repairs like replacing damaged boards?
faqs.answer: Never bundle major repairs into your square metre sanding price. Quote them as a separate item with a clear description of the work. Charge your standard hourly rate (e.g., $70-$90/hour) plus the cost of materials. Sourcing and matching aged timber can be time-consuming, so make sure your labour charge reflects that effort. This keeps the sanding quote clean and protects you from unknown costs.

window-replacement-quote-template.intro: This window replacement quote template is for glaziers doing residential jobs, from single swaps to whole-house refits. Most quotes get the new window price right but lose money on two things: the labour for making good on internal plaster and architraves, and the real cost of disposing of old frames and glass. This template helps you price those items correctly so your final figure covers the whole job, not just the new unit. Getting the details straight means you price fairly, protect your margin, and avoid arguments with the client when the job is done.

sections.heading: How to Price Labour and Materials for a Window Swap
sections.body: Your main costs are the window unit and your time. A standard 1200x1200mm aluminium window from a supplier like Stegbar or Bradnams might cost $450-$600 plus GST. Labour is the biggest variable. A simple swap in a brick veneer home takes 2-3 hours. If it's a second-storey job or a difficult opening, budget 4-5 hours. At an $90/hour rate, that’s a big difference. Add consumables like a tube of SikaFlex PRO sealant ($25 at a trade supplier) and flashing tape. Always add a 10% contingency on materials. Your base cost for that single window swap is closer to $800 before you add your margin.

sections.heading: What Gets Left Off a Window Replacement Quote
sections.body: Forgetting disposal fees is the most common mistake. A trip to the tip with old frames and glass can cost $80-$150. Second is access equipment. If the window is on an upper floor, you'll need to quote for scaffold or scissor lift hire, which can be $300+ per day. Third is making good. Clearly state if your price includes patching and painting internal plaster reveals and architraves. If not, specify that it's the client's responsibility. Finally, always note that the installation complies with Australian Standard AS 2047, which covers things like structural integrity and water penetration.

faqs.question: How much extra should I quote for a custom-sized window?
faqs.answer: Custom-sized windows typically cost 25-50% more from the manufacturer than a standard size. You should also add at least two extra hours of labour to your quote for the careful installation and finishing they require. Make sure you get a confirmed price and lead time from your supplier, like A&L Windows, before you send the final quote to the customer.

faqs.question: Do I need to include scaffolding hire in my quote?
faqs.answer: Yes, if any part of the window is over two metres from the ground, you need a safe work platform. List scaffold hire as a separate line item. A small mobile tower from a hire place like Kennards can cost $150-$250 for a day. If you don't quote it, that cost comes directly out of your profit. It's a non-negotiable safety item.

faqs.question: What's the standard for waterproofing a new window?
faqs.answer: The installation must comply with AS 2047. This involves installing flexible flashing tape around the entire window opening before the frame goes in, especially in brick veneer. Relying just on a bead of sealant is not enough and will lead to leaks. Use a quality product like Grace Vycor Plus flashing tape to meet the National Construction Code requirements.

power-point-installation-quote-template.intro: This power point installation quote template is for Australian electricians quoting standard GPO jobs. It suits everything from adding a single point in a bedroom to a multi-point kitchen fit-out. The biggest mistakes are underquoting labour for tricky access, especially in brick walls, and forgetting to factor in travel time for a small job. A single GPO install can become unprofitable if you don't account for the drive. This template helps you price every line item correctly, from the GPO itself to the cable runs and wall clips, ensuring you don't lose your margin.

sections.heading: How to Price Labour and Materials for GPO Installs
sections.body: Labour is the biggest variable. Installing a GPO in a plasterboard wall with good roof or floor access might take 30-45 minutes. The same job on an internal double-brick wall could take 2-3 hours, requiring chasing, conduit, and patching. Your labour rate should reflect this. Materials are more fixed. A standard Clipsal 2000 series double GPO costs about $12 from Middy's. Add $2-$3 per metre for 2.5mm twin and earth cable from a trade supplier. A simple plasterboard install might be quoted at $180, while the brick wall equivalent could be over $400. A quoting app like QuoteMate lets you save different labour rates for each scenario.

sections.heading: What Gets Left Off a GPO Installation Quote
sections.body: Forgetting to check the existing circuit load is a common mistake. If the circuit is already maxed out, you'll need to quote for a new run back to the switchboard and a new circuit breaker. This adds significant cost. Also, specify who handles plaster patching and painting. If you don't do it, state that clearly. For brick walls, always include line items for conduit and the extra time for wall chasing. Finally, confirm the new work will be covered by a safety switch (RCD). If not, you must quote to install one at the switchboard to comply with AS/NZS 3000.

faqs.question: Do I need to quote for a safety switch on every new power point?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the circuit you're connecting to isn't already protected. All new socket outlets must have RCD protection under AS/NZS 3000. Forgetting to check and quote for a new RCBO at the switchboard can cost you $50-$80 in materials plus an hour of labour.

faqs.question: How much extra is a GPO with USB ports?
faqs.answer: The GPO unit itself is the main difference. A standard Clipsal double GPO might be $12, but a USB-C version like the Clipsal Iconic can be over $70 from an electrical wholesaler. The installation labour is identical, so just add the higher material cost plus your markup to the quote.

faqs.question: What's a fair travel or call-out fee for a single GPO job?
faqs.answer: For one power point, a minimum charge is essential. Many sparkies set a minimum of one hour's labour, around $90-$120, plus a service vehicle fee of $50 to cover travel costs. State this minimum charge clearly on the quote so the customer knows the base price.

turf-laying-quote-template.intro: This is for landscapers pricing residential turf jobs. It's a turf supply & lay quote template designed for common projects like new builds or backyard makeovers. Most tradies get tripped up on two things: underestimating the labour for site prep, and forgetting the cost of dumping the old lawn and soil. A 2m³ skip bin can cost $350 before you’ve even laid a roll of turf. This template helps you price every step, from the initial weed kill to the final roll, so your margin is protected and the client knows exactly what they’re paying for.

sections.heading: How to Calculate Costs for Turf Supply and Lay
sections.body: Your price is built from four key costs: turf, soil, labour, and disposal. First, the turf itself. Sir Walter Buffalo from a turf farm will run you about $15-$18 per square metre. Next, topsoil. You’ll need at least 50mm of quality underlay, which costs around $90 per cubic metre from a landscape supplier, plus delivery. Labour for a two-person crew is about $120-$150 per hour. A standard 80m² job can take 6-8 hours for prep and laying. Finally, waste disposal. Hiring a turf cutter from a trade supplier is about $120 a day, and a skip bin for the old grass will add another $250-$400 depending on its size.

sections.heading: Mistakes That Kill Your Margin on Turf Jobs
sections.body: The biggest mistake is quoting for turf but forgetting the prep work. Your quote must include line items for initial glyphosate spraying, hiring a turf cutter, and the labour to strip the site. Another costly error is ignoring site access. If you can’t get a wheelbarrow to the backyard easily, your labour hours will blow out. Add an 'access fee' or increase your labour allowance for difficult sites. Also, specify a soil depth on your quote. Promising a 'new lawn' is vague. Stating you will 'supply and spread 75mm of premium topsoil' is a fixed scope. This prevents the client asking for more soil later without a variation.

faqs.question: How much waste factor should I add for turf?
faqs.answer: Always add 5-10% to your turf order for cuts and wastage. If the area has a lot of curves around garden beds or paths, lean towards 10%. For a simple 100m² rectangular yard, ordering 105m² of turf gives you a safe buffer for offcuts without leaving you short on the job.

faqs.question: Do I charge for site prep separately on the quote?
faqs.answer: No, build it into the total price but list it as line items. Show the client the cost for 'Site clearing with turf cutter' and 'Waste disposal via 2m³ skip bin'. This shows the value you're providing and justifies your price, preventing arguments over work that isn't just the turf itself. A day's turf cutter hire from Kennards is about $110.

faqs.question: What's the right way to price the soil?
faqs.answer: Price soil by the cubic metre (m³), including delivery. A healthy lawn needs a base of at least 50-100mm of quality topsoil. For a 100m² area needing 50mm of soil, you'll need 5m³ (100m² x 0.05m). Get a current price from your local landscape supplier like ANL, as delivery fees can add another $50-$100 to the material cost.

hedge-trimming-quote-template.intro: This hedge trimming quote template suits most residential and body corporate jobs, from simple boundary hedges to more complex shaping. It helps you price jobs accurately so you don't lose money on the two items most landscapers forget: green waste disposal and difficult site access. Quoting these correctly from the start prevents arguments with the client later. Use this hedge trimming quote template to make sure your labour, gear, and disposal costs are covered every time, leaving you with a decent margin for your work.

sections.heading: How to Price Hedge Trimming: By the Metre vs. By the Hour
sections.body: For standard jobs, pricing per linear metre is fastest. For a typical 2-metre high lilly pilly or photinia hedge, charge $20-$40 per metre, one side. Double it for both sides. If it's overgrown, tangled, or needs a serious height reduction, switch to an hourly rate. Charge $70-$100 per hour, per person on site. This covers you for unexpected challenges. Remember to factor in fuel for the trimmer and blower, plus blade sharpening costs. A can of 2-stroke oil from a trade supplier is around $15, so make sure your hourly rate covers all your running costs.

sections.heading: What Gets Left Off: Tip Fees and Tricky Site Access
sections.body: Green waste disposal is a real cost. A packed ute or trailer load of clippings can cost you $90-$160 at a commercial waste facility. Always include a separate line item for 'Waste Removal and Tip Fees' so the client sees what they're paying for. Also, price for access. If you have to park on the street and haul clippings 50 metres through a narrow gate, that's extra labour. Add 15-25% to your labour time for poor access. For hedges over 3 metres high, you might need scaffolding or a cherry picker, which must be quoted as a separate hire cost.

faqs.question: How much should I charge for green waste removal?
faqs.answer: Price it as a separate line item based on volume. A standard 6x4 trailer or ute tray load costs between $90 and $160 at most council tips for commercial green waste. If you're doing a big job that will fill the truck, call your local waste management centre for their current price per tonne to ensure you're covered.

faqs.question: Do I charge more for formal shaping or topiary work?
faqs.answer: Yes. A straight trim is priced per metre or hour. Detailed shaping is a skilled, slow process that should be quoted as a fixed price per plant or section. It requires more precision and time than a standard cut. Your rate for this detailed work should be at least double your standard hourly rate to reflect the higher skill level involved.

faqs.question: What's the best way to handle a client who wants to keep the clippings?
faqs.answer: Confirm exactly where they want them piled and state this on the quote. Specify that you will cut and drop, but not move or spread the clippings. If they want you to move the clippings to a compost heap at the back of the property, you must charge for that labour time. Clearly separating these tasks on the quote avoids disputes.

cabinet-door-replacement-quote-template.intro: This cabinet door replacement quote template is for cabinet-makers doing kitchen and laundry refreshes. It suits jobs where the cabinet carcasses are sound, but the doors and drawer fronts need a modern look. Most tradies get quotes wrong in two places: underestimating the labour for adjusting hinges on old or out-of-square cabinets, and completely forgetting to charge for the disposal of the old doors. This template helps you price every component accurately, from the Polytec board and Blum hinges right through to cleanup, ensuring your quote is fair for the client and profitable for you.

sections.heading: How to Price Labour and Materials for a Door Swap
sections.body: The main costs are board material and your time. A standard Polytec Woodmatt sheet (2400x1200mm) costs around $180-$250 from a trade supplier. Calculate your door sizes, add a 15% waste factor, and price the board accordingly. Labour is the tricky part. Don't charge by the hour; charge per door. A good rate is $70-$90 per door. This covers the site measure, removing old doors, installing new hinges, hanging the new door, and the final alignment. This per-unit price protects you if you hit a stubborn cabinet that needs extra work. Using a tool like QuoteMate helps you itemise each door and apply consistent pricing instantly.

sections.heading: What Gets Left Off a Cabinet Door Quote
sections.body: Forgetting small items kills your profit. Always check if new handles or knobs are needed, as clients often assume they're included. A simple handle from a trade supplier can be $8, but architectural handles can be over $50 each. Also, add a line item for 'Hardware Sundries' to cover screws, packers, and bumpers. Disposal is another big one; a trip to the tip isn't free. Add a minimum $100 charge for removing and legally disposing of the old doors and any packaging. Finally, if the job requires new soft-close hinges like Blum Inserta, price them individually at around $7-$10 per hinge, not as part of the general labour cost.

faqs.question: Should I add markup on materials like Polytec board and hinges?
faqs.answer: Yes, always add a markup to cover your time sourcing materials, handling, and storage. A standard markup on materials for a cabinet-maker is between 20% and 30%. This is an industry-standard practice and ensures you aren't just a free procurement service for the client. Your quote should show a single supply price, not your cost plus markup.

faqs.question: How do I quote for replacing drawer fronts as well as doors?
faqs.answer: Price drawer fronts separately. They require more labour than a simple hinged door because you have to mount them to the drawer box and align them perfectly with adjacent doors and drawers. A good rule is to charge about 25% more for a drawer front installation than a standard door. For example, if your door rate is $80, charge $100 per drawer front.

faqs.question: Is there an Australian Standard for replacing cabinet doors?
faqs.answer: There is no specific standard just for replacing doors. However, your work should still align with the principles of good workmanship found in AS/NZS 4386.1 for domestic kitchen assemblies. This mainly relates to ensuring hinges are fitted correctly, doors are aligned with safe gaps, and are fit for purpose. Mentioning your work meets industry best practice is enough for the quote.

leaf-guard-installation-quote-template.intro: Quoting leaf guard installation looks simple, but it's easy to get stung. This leaf guard installation quote template is built for Aussie roofers doing standard residential jobs on tile or metal roofs. The main things guys get wrong are underestimating labour on steep pitches—anything over 25 degrees needs extra time and safety gear—and not factoring enough waste for complex rooflines with multiple hips and valleys. Get the measurements and labour right, and you protect your profit. This template helps you price every screw and metre of mesh correctly, so you're not working for free on the tricky bits.

sections.heading: How to Price Leaf Guard Labour and Materials
sections.body: Price leaf guard jobs per linear metre, but adjust for complexity. A simple single-storey brick veneer might be $35-$55 per metre. This covers materials like All-Flow aluminium mesh from a trade supplier, which runs about $10-$15 per metre, plus screws and silicone. Your labour is the biggest variable. A steep roof (over 30 degrees) or a two-storey house immediately adds 20-30% to your labour time due to harness work and extra safety precautions. Don't forget to price valleys separately; they use wider mesh and take longer to fit correctly. For a standard 60-metre home, always budget for at least 5% material waste.

sections.heading: What Most Roofers Forget on a Leaf Guard Quote
sections.body: The biggest mistake is not charging for gutter cleaning. It's not part of the installation, it's a separate line item. A gutter full of wet sludge can add hours to the job. Always quote 'Gutter clean prior to installation' separately, usually $4-$6 per metre. Another forgotten cost is rubbish removal; a standard house can generate 3-4 large bags of debris. Also, factor in access. A two-storey job or a steep pitch might require edge protection or scaffolding hire, adding $500-$1500 to the cost. Forgetting this will wipe out your entire profit. All work at height must use gear that meets AS/NZS 1891 standards.

faqs.question: Do I charge more for tile roofs than metal roofs?
faqs.answer: Yes, slightly. Tiled roofs often require more precise trimming of the mesh to sit correctly under the second course of tiles, and the saddles or clips can take longer to install than screwing directly to a metal roof's gutter lip. Add around 10-15% to your labour calculation for a standard concrete tile roof compared to a Colorbond roof.

faqs.question: What's the best way to measure up a leaf guard job?
faqs.answer: Measure every straight run of guttering with a laser measure or tape and add them up for a total linear metre count. Don't just measure the house footprint. Walk the perimeter and measure the valleys separately as they require wider, more expensive mesh. For a typical 4-bedroom house, expect around 50-70 linear metres of guttering.

faqs.question: Should I include a warranty on my leaf guard installation?
faqs.answer: Yes, offer a warranty on your workmanship, typically 12-24 months. This covers screws coming loose or sections lifting. The material itself usually has a manufacturer's warranty, like the 15-year warranty on Gumleaf gutter guard. Make sure your quote specifies that your warranty covers installation labour only, not product failure or storm damage.

gutter-cleaning-quote-template.intro: This gutter cleaning quote template is for roofers pricing residential jobs, from single-storey homes to townhouses. Most tradies get tripped up on two things: underestimating the time it takes to work safely on a two-storey roof and completely forgetting to charge for waste disposal. This template makes sure you account for both. Get your labour rates and disposal fees right, and you'll make a profit on every job. It’s built for Aussie roofers who want to send a professional quote in minutes without missing key costs.

sections.heading: How to Price Gutter Cleaning Per Metre
