sections.body: Most experienced roofers charge by the linear metre. For a single-storey house with easy ladder access, $7 to $12 per metre is a common range in major cities. For a two-storey or steep-pitched roof, that can easily jump to $15 to $25 per metre because of the extra safety setup and time. Always have a minimum call-out fee, around $220-$300, to make small jobs worthwhile. This rate should cover your labour, gear, and consumables like heavy-duty refuse bags. A 10-pack of 100L rubble bags costs about $10, so your per-metre rate must absorb these costs.

sections.heading: Forgetting Access and Disposal Costs Will Kill Your Profit
sections.body: The biggest mistake is not quoting for difficult access and waste disposal. If the roof pitch is over 25 degrees or it's a two-storey building, you may need temporary edge protection or a full harness system to comply with Safe Work Australia guidelines. This hire cost must be on the quote. The other forgotten cost is the local tip fee. A ute-load of wet leaves and sludge is heavy, and your council tip will charge for it. This can be anywhere from $80 to $150. A quoting tool like QuoteMate lets you save these as standard line items so you never forget to include them.

faqs.question: Should I charge extra to clean gutters with guards on them?
faqs.answer: Yes, always. Removing and refitting gutter guards can double the labour time. Add a separate line item for it. A good rule of thumb is to add 30-50% to your per-metre labour rate for any lengths covered by guards. Make sure the customer understands this charge before you start, so there are no surprises on the final invoice.

faqs.question: Is flushing downpipes included in a standard gutter clean?
faqs.answer: It should be an optional line item. A basic water flush to check for flow is often included, but clearing a serious blockage is a different task. Specify on your quote that a basic flush is covered, but significant blockages will be quoted separately. This manages expectations and follows the stormwater maintenance principles outlined in AS/NZS 3500.3.

faqs.question: What if I find broken tiles or rust during the clean?
faqs.answer: Your quote's scope should state it only covers the clean. Note that you will report any damage found, and repairs can be quoted as a separate job. This protects you from doing unpaid work and positions you as a helpful expert. Always take photos of any damage to show the client when you present the quote for the extra repair work.

general-pest-control-quote-template.intro: This general pest control quote template is for standard residential jobs: spiders, ants, and common cockroaches in a typical three-bedroom house. The biggest mistakes pesties make are under-quoting chemical costs for large perimeters and not allowing enough time for a thorough job, especially in cluttered roof voids or subfloors. Get those two things right, and you’ll stop losing money on your bread-and-butter work. This template provides the line items to make sure every litre of chemical and every minute on site is covered in your price.

sections.heading: How to Price a Standard Residential Pest Spray
sections.body: A standard 3-bedder takes about 1 to 1.5 hours on site. At a charge-out rate of $150/hr, that's up to $225 in labour. Your main chemical is a bifenthrin concentrate, like the 1L bottles from Agserv or Garrards. A bottle might cost you $80 and make 100L of spray at the general pest rate. If you use 10L per job, your chemical cost is $8. Add another $20 for vehicle running costs and consumables like gloves and masks. Your base cost is around $253 before markup and GST. An app like QuoteMate helps track these costs job-to-job.

sections.heading: What Gets Left Off: German Cockroaches and Poor Access
sections.body: A general spray price doesn't cover every situation. German cockroach infestations are a classic error; they need specific gel baits and often a follow-up visit, which must be quoted as a separate, higher-priced service. Always add a line item for difficult access, like clearing a blocked manhole or working in a tight subfloor. A client's packed garage isn't your fault, so charge for the extra half-hour of labour it costs you. Also, specify the warranty period on the quote, like a 6-month service-free period for spiders, to manage expectations. All treatments must comply with the label directions approved by the APVMA.

faqs.question: How much extra should I charge for a two-storey house?
faqs.answer: A two-storey house adds time for moving equipment and managing ladder safety, plus it has a larger external perimeter and more eaves to treat. A good rule of thumb is to add 30-50% to your standard single-storey price. If your base job is $300, quote at least $390 for the two-storey version.

faqs.question: Do I need to quote differently for an end-of-lease spray?
faqs.answer: Yes. An end-of-lease spray is usually for a vacant and clean property, making access easier and the job faster. You can often price it 10-15% lower than for an occupied home. The quote should specify it only covers the property as-is, as required by the real estate agent.

faqs.question: Is a German cockroach job priced the same as a general spray?
faqs.answer: No, and quoting it the same is a quick way to lose money. A German roach job requires specialised gel baits, like Maxforce Gold, and insect growth regulators. It also often requires a follow-up visit. Price this as a separate service, typically costing at least 50% more than a general spray.

fence-repair-quote-template.intro: A fence repair seems simple until you're digging out an old concrete footing by hand. Underquote that labour and you've lost your profit for the day. This fence repair quote template is for Australian fencers tackling common jobs like replacing rotted posts, storm-damaged palings, or sagging sections. Most fencers get caught out by forgetting to quote for tip fees to dispose of the old treated pine and concrete, or not factoring in enough time for tricky site access. We've built this template to cover those hidden costs so your quote is accurate from the start.

sections.heading: Calculating Costs for Posts, Palings, and Labour
sections.body: The real cost in a fence repair is labour, not materials. Don't quote by the hour; quote per post or per metre. Digging out and replacing a single rotted post can take 2-3 hours, so budget at least $200 in labour for just one. For materials, a 90x90mm H4 treated pine post from a trade supplier runs about $35, plus $10 for a bag of Rapid Set concrete. Standard 1.8m palings are cheap at around $3.50 each, but always add a 10% waste factor for splits and offcuts. For a typical three-post, ten-paling repair, your base material cost will be around $150 before markup.

sections.heading: Hidden Costs: Site Access and Waste Disposal
sections.body: Two costs kill your profit on small repairs: waste disposal and site access. Old treated pine and concrete footings can't just go in the bin. A trip to the tip with a ute-load will cost you $80 to $150, so add a line item for 'Waste Removal'. Second, check the access. If you're carting concrete bags and posts 50 metres up a sloping backyard, add a 'Difficult Access Surcharge' to your labour. It's also a mistake not to check for underground services before you dig. A quick check on the Dial Before You Dig website is free and saves you from hitting a water pipe.

faqs.question: Should I charge a call-out fee for a small fence repair quote?
faqs.answer: Yes, for jobs under a few hundred dollars, a call-out fee of $80-$120 is standard. It covers your travel time and expertise if the customer doesn't proceed. Be upfront about it, and offer to waive it if they accept the quote. This filters out tyre-kickers and ensures you're paid for your time. Most genuine customers understand you have to cover your fuel and an hour of your day.

faqs.question: How much markup should I add to materials for a fence repair?
faqs.answer: For small repair jobs, a 20-25% markup on materials is typical. This covers your time sourcing parts from a trade supplier or a local timber yard, plus handling. On a larger job you might reduce this to 15%, but for a handful of posts and palings, a 25% margin is fair and standard industry practice.

faqs.question: Do I need to specify the exact type of screws in the quote?
faqs.answer: Yes, be specific. It shows professionalism and justifies your cost. List 'Galvanised Bugle Batten Screws 14g x 100mm' for rails, not just 'screws'. This prevents arguments about using cheap fasteners that will rust. Specifying quality galvanised hardware from a trade supplier shows you aren't cutting corners and builds trust with the client.

rodent-control-quote-template.intro: This rodent control quote template is for residential and light commercial jobs. It covers standard baiting and trapping for rats and mice in houses, sheds, and small offices. The biggest mistake pesties make is quoting a flat fee without seeing the site. A small unit is different from a large house with a cluttered roof space. The other classic error is forgetting to price the follow-up visits. This template helps you itemise everything so you get paid for all the work you do.

sections.heading: How to Price Baiting, Trapping, and Labour
sections.body: The cost is driven by materials and time. A standard lockable bait station from Agserv or Garrards costs about $10-$15. You'll need 4-6 for a typical house exterior. A bucket of Contrac Blox might be $100, but you only use a few blocks per station. The real variable is labour. A standard call-out fee for the first hour is usually $220-$300 including GST. This covers the initial inspection and setup. Any follow-up visits should be quoted separately, typically at a lower rate like $120 per visit, as they're quicker checks and re-baits.

sections.heading: What Gets Left Off a Rodent Control Quote
sections.body: Always quote for follow-up visits. Most jobs need at least one check at the 2-week mark to assess activity and rebait. Forgetting this line item means you do it for free. Also, consider adding rodent-proofing as an optional extra. This involves blocking entry points with steel wool or sealant and is a separate charge. Difficult access is another one. If you need to crawl through a tight roof void or under a low deck, add a labour charge for the extra time. Finally, factor in safe disposal of any carcasses, as this is part of the service covered by the AEPMA Code of Practice.

faqs.question: How much should I charge for a follow-up visit?
faqs.answer: A follow-up is shorter than the initial setup, so charge less. A common rate is a fixed fee between $90 and $150 plus GST. This should cover up to 30 minutes on site for checking stations, removing any carcasses, and topping up bait. Always state the cost for follow-ups clearly on your initial quote.

faqs.question: Should I include rodent-proofing in the main quote?
faqs.answer: No, quote it as a separate, optional line item. Rodent-proofing is a construction task, not a pest control task. It uses different materials and skills. Separating it gives the customer a clear choice and protects your margin if they only want the baiting service. You can source proofing mesh and fillers from trade suppliers.

faqs.question: Do I need to add GST to my rodent control quote?
faqs.answer: Yes, if your business is registered for GST, you must add 10% to the total price. Pest control services are not GST-free in Australia. Forgetting it means you pay the 10% out of your own pocket. Using software like QuoteMate automatically calculates and adds GST to every line item, ensuring your invoices are always correct.
